raw.title: Credit Analyst
raw.description:
About 9fin

9fin is the AI platform powering global debt markets — the world’s largest asset class at over $145 trillion.

Debt markets are vast, global, and mission-critical, yet still run on fragmented data, PDFs, and manual workflows. 9fin replaces this broken infrastructure with a single platform that centralises proprietary credit data, deep analysis, and high-value workflows across global markets.

Today, 9fin powers teams at 300+ blue-chip institutions worldwide, including global banks, asset managers, private equity firms, law firms, and advisors. The business is scaling at exceptional speed, with rapid expansion in the US and best-in-class retention driven by deep workflow adoption.

We’re at a defining inflection point. With proven product-market fit and strong, global market pull, 9fin is accelerating toward becoming the category-defining platform for debt markets worldwide.

What you’ll work on

Every day is different, but here’s an example of the kind of things you’ll work on:

  • Primary analysis – Review new debt transactions in the high yield and leveraged loan market, ensuring we produce quick and insightful reports

  • Secondary analysis – With guidance from senior analysts, deep dive into high yield earnings reports, provide financial updates on specific credits, and produce market-leading predictive analysis and industry research

  • Relationship & product evangelism – Support clients, answer questions on our platform and provide insight. Gather feedback and work with the product team to develop the 9fin offering, taking the lead on new and exciting developments

About You

This role will be a great fit if you demonstrate:

  • A strong interest in financial markets, and a desire to learn about how they work

  • Strong communication and writing skills – Demonstrate clear and effective written and verbal communication, producing clean, timely, and accurate copy in a concise manner. Exhibit excellent attention to detail

  • Problem solving – Enjoy interpreting information and constructing effective solutions to complex problems. Be a team player, but also able to effectively work alone (although help is always on hand if you need)

  • Drive – Bring an inquisitive and passionate mindset, demonstrating a strong interest in the development and dynamics of financial (and especially) capital markets. A self-starter, you are up for the challenge of a role that will morph and transform as we continue to grow

We’re open to candidates from a range of backgrounds – if you’re curious, analytical, and enjoy working with financial data, we’d love to hear from you!

Our benefits

We’re a scaling start up and we enjoy sharing our success, when the company succeeds, we always reinvest that in our people. We also offer huge amounts of responsibility, an abundance of opportunity for growth and a platform to truly excel.

Financial & Insurance

  • Competitive salary benchmarked at 75-90th% of market

  • Pension (your minimum contributions are 4% with 9fin matching up to 7%)

  • Private Medical Insurance

  • Paid sick leave with Income Protection for long periods of illness

  • Group Life Assurance

  • Season Ticket Loan & Cycle to Work schemes

Time off

  • 25 holiday days per year

  • Local public holidays (with the ability to exchange them for alternative days)

  • Work abroad for up to 3 months a year

  • 1 month paid sabbatical after 5 years of service

  • Enhanced parental leave & flexible working arrangements available

Training & Culture

  • Professional learning and development budget

  • Quarterly team socials

  • Summer and Winter company social events

Hybrid Policy

9fin is a hybrid company, and the office is a regular part of how we work. From January 2027, all employees will work from their designated 9fin office on Tuesdays and Wednesdays. Some teams may be asked to be in the office more often, where the nature of their work calls for it. For the rest of the week, you may work from wherever works best for you and your team. Your Talent Partner will share hybrid working details for this role.

9fin is an equal opportunities employer

At 9fin we are dedicated to building and promoting a fair and inclusive workplace where everyone can reach their full potential and truly belong. We recognize that building diverse teams enables a more creative and productive environment. If you’re excited about this role but your experience doesn’t perfectly align with the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You might just be who we’re looking for — either for this role, or perhaps another.

At 9fin, we've built a dedicated Data Operations team in Belfast to enhance our data processing capabilities.

You'll work closely with teams in New York, London, and Belfast across Leveraged Finance, Structured Credit, Private Credit, and Distressed Debt.

Every day brings new challenges, and the team’s responsibilities will continue to expand.

Associate - News & Market Data Team

Providing fast, reliable news and market data across a wide range of financial markets is no small task. Our team uses cutting-edge technology to source, analyse, and publish the most relevant information for our clients.

  • Leverage proprietary technology – Understand and navigate HTML, using 9fin’s in-house tools to automate publishing and streamline data workflows.

  • Monitor and review market-moving news – Identify price-sensitive information in articles surfaced by our in-house aggregator.

  • Track financial results and company performance – Ensure timely updates on earnings publications and corporate disclosures.

You’ll be responsible for monitoring and recording key reporting dates, ensuring they are accurately tracked and updated on internal and client facing platforms.

  • Monitor redemptions and maturities – Conduct checks on bond and loan redemptions, updating relevant datasets and client alerts.

  • Curiosity about financial markets and business – While prior knowledge isn’t required, you have a keen interest in how markets, companies, and financial news interact.

  • Willingness to challenge the status quo – You see how things could be done better and aren’t afraid to speak up with ideas for improvement.

raw.title: Head Of Data Protection & DPO
raw.description:
💬 Accurx is solving healthcare productivity for the NHS.

For decades, the NHS has struggled with fragmented systems that make simple tasks feel impossible. At Accurx, we’re changing that by building a single, system-wide platform that helps every patient get gold-standard, efficient, and joined-up care.

What started as a way for GPs to text a patient has now evolved into an all-in-one digital toolkit used by 98% of GP practices.

Our platform now powers Total Triage to manage patient demand, and Self-Book, which lets patients schedule their own appointments in seconds. We’ve automated routine care with Patient Questionnaires for long-term conditions, while Accumail finally allows staff-to-staff communication to happen instantly across different care settings. We’re now pushing the boundaries of the consultation itself with Accurx Scribe, our AI-powered note-taker that drafts medical notes in real-time.

We’re not just shipping features. We’re giving clinicians their time back and ensuring every patient journey is as smooth as it should be.


The Opportunity:

We're on a journey to steward AI into the NHS safely and responsibly. We've already deployed ambient voice technology to write up consultations, released our first AI triage products to help practices read and route hundreds of patient requests a day, and we're now working on deploying agents in healthcare settings.

The next few years will define how AI is used with patient data in the NHS. As Head of Data Protection and our in-house DPO, you'll help set that standard nationally: building the frameworks that let us move quickly and safely, and earning the trust of the patients, clinicians and organisations who rely on us.

This role is about building and shaping, not just running. You'll own data protection at Accurx end to end: the strategy, the statutory role, the team and the calls. You'll be a key leader in our Technology division, working as a trusted partner to our Chief Product Officer and Head of Legal.

Challenges you'll solve...

  • Steward AI into the NHS: set Accurx's positions on how we build, deploy and monitor AI products at scale, from controllership and assistive vs automated, to retention of AI inputs and outputs, sub-processors and model hosting, without ever undermining the trust we've built with our users

  • Set guardrails, not gates: define clear guardrails so product teams can move fast inside them without asking permission each time, and make our positions public and credible so NHS DPOs can rely on them rather than starting from scratch

  • Bring privacy into product design: work with product, design and engineering to embed privacy by design. Much of what we're building hasn't been seen in the health system before, so you'll need to be unapologetically forward-looking and comfortable taking informed, calculated risks

  • Turn decisions into reusable patterns: with our in-house privacy team, build governance templates, pre-approved data flows and plain-English privacy notice wording that healthcare organisations can pick up and use, and shape how we responsibly use our data to improve products and patient outcomes

  • Hold the statutory DPO role with independence: inform, advise and monitor compliance under UK GDPR, including our record of processing, DPIAs, training and audits. You'll be our named contact for the ICO, NHS customers and data subjects, and lead testing, breach assessment and reporting

  • Run corporate privacy: own our core privacy obligations and registrations, keep the evidence current for regulators, customers and bids, lead privacy due diligence on suppliers, partners and corporate transactions, and oversee how we handle employee and corporate data as well as patient data

  • Build a function that moves at product speed: lead and grow a small, bar-raising privacy and data function, and make it easy for 200+ colleagues to get fast, consistent answers to privacy questions

You should apply if...

  • You're product-minded about privacy: you've worked inside a product company and helped ship things, finding an approach that's both more private and better for the user. You've guided technology organisations through responsible innovation, especially where AI/ML meets sensitive data

  • You're AI-fluent with deep UK data protection expertise: you apply UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018, the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 and the common law duty of confidentiality in practice, understand how modern AI systems actually handle data, and have a view on ICO AI guidance and where regulation is heading

  • You've built and led privacy teams: you grow capability, bring your team into decisions, delegate real ownership and build trust across functions

  • You're confident externally: you can represent the business to regulators, NHS organisations and partners, and communicate complex positions clearly

  • You know health and the NHS, or have a fast route to it: controller and processor roles in primary care, DSPT, DTAC, the Caldicott Principles and the national data opt-out. You learn the NHS by going to see it

  • You challenge the status quo: you stay ahead of changes in digital health, AI and data ethics, and see privacy as something that enables the business to move at pace

What’s in it for you?

You’ll join a high-performing team on a mission to solve healthcare productivity, building a platform used by around 300k NHS staff every week, supporting the care of over 50 million NHS patients every year. We set a high bar, move fast, and give people the ownership and support to do the best work of their careers

  • £110,000 - £140,000 salary, plus a discretionary recognition bonus for exceptional performance and impact, nominated by managers and awarded by our leadership team

  • Equity: £100,000 in equal share options, so you share in the value you help create

  • Benefits to suit you: adjust your healthcare cover, your pension or life insurance, whatever stage you’re at in life

  • Built for collaboration: We are an office-first culture and ask that you’re in our (dog-friendly) Shoreditch office for a minimum of 3 days a week

  • Close to our users: Regular hackathons, plus dedicated time to visit GP practices and other healthcare settings to see first-hand how our products are used

  • Time off: You’ll get 28 days of holiday (plus bank holidays) and up to 4 weeks to work from anywhere per year

  • Support at home: We offer enhanced parental leave, fertility support and parental loss support

  • We have our very own chefs: Free healthy breakfasts, snacks and lunches, plus a weekly sweet treat

Compensation: £110K – £140K • Offers Equity

How you'll make impact

We’re looking for an Account Executive to help ambitious mid-market businesses solve complex financial and billing challenges. You’ll own the customer relationship from first conversation through close, partnering with internal teams to set each opportunity up for success.

  • Own the full sales cycle for mid-market customers, from prospecting and territory planning through negotiation and close.

  • Drive new customer acquisition and revenue growth by helping businesses solve complex financial and billing challenges.

  • Build trusted relationships with senior stakeholders, including CXOs, and represent Airwallex in customer meetings and events.

  • Translate complex customer requirements into solutions across Airwallex’s products.

  • Maintain accurate CRM activity and forecasting so the team has a clear view of pipeline, priorities and performance.

You’ll work from our London office three days a week.

What we're looking for

Essentials

  • 2+ years of experience in outbound business development.

  • 1+ years of experience in a closing capacity.

  • Experience selling a billing tool or similar product.

  • A track record of strong sales performance and hitting targets.

  • Experience owning a full sales cycle, from prospecting through close.

  • The ability to understand complex technical requirements and craft solutions across multiple products.

  • Strong presentation and communication skills, particularly in person with multiple senior stakeholders.

  • Superior verbal and written communication skills in English.

Preferred

  • Experience working with mid-market customers.

  • Experience in fintech, payments, SaaS or another highly regulated or technically complex environment.

  • Experience creating and executing territory plans.

  • Experience representing a company at customer events, with some travel required.

You'll thrive here if

  • You have a track record of hitting your numbers, and you're motivated by stretch goals.

  • You're comfortable owning the roadmap yourself.

  • You own the outcome and you don't wait for permission to fix what's broken.

  • You communicate clearly and directly across cultures, and you're thoughtful about how context shifts meaning across borders.

  • You say what you mean. You're direct, but you lead with respect.

Learn more about your team

SME & Growth at Airwallex is about more than closing deals. We help small and mid-market businesses solve real financial challenges across borders: getting paid globally, managing multi-currency accounts, paying suppliers, and running spend across markets from a single platform. You're not selling a feature. You're helping founders and finance leaders replace fragmented financial operations with one global system that actually scales.

It's a function for sellers who like to build, not follow a script: curious, resourceful, and comfortable figuring things out in markets that are still wide open. You get real autonomy to create value, build relationships, and move opportunities forward.

If you want to sell a serious product, solve real problems for ambitious businesses, and build your career fast, this is a place to do it.

Search firms/recruiters submitting resumes to Airwallex on an unsolicited basis shall be deemed to accept this condition, regardless of any other provision to the contrary.

Equal opportunity

Airwallex is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and anyone seeking employment at Airwallex is considered based on merit, qualifications, competence and talent. raw.description:
About Airwallex

Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. More than 675,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own.

We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,700 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do. Read our operating principles to see it in full.

 

Who you are

We are looking for an Associate Director, Payments/Scheme Economics to own the integrity, visibility and management of Airwallex’s payment costs, starting with card scheme fees and interchange fees across Visa and Mastercard.

Reporting to the Head of Strategic Finance, you will be the subject matter expert on scheme economics, translating complex and rapidly changing network rules into accurate system configurations, financial outcomes and business decisions. You will ensure we understand what every payment should cost, that those costs are accurately reflected across our systems and financials, and that we systematically identify opportunities to improve payment economics as we scale.

Over time, the remit will expand across other card schemes, local payment methods and the broader payments cost base.

What you’ll do

  • Own scheme economics and rule interpretation: Maintain deep expertise across scheme fees, interchange and network rules. Interpret scheme bulletins, operating regulations and fee schedules, translating changes into clear financial, product and operational requirements.

  • Ensure accurate payment cost configuration: Translate complex scheme rules into fee tables, eligibility criteria and transaction-level logic. Partner with Product and Engineering to ensure cost calculation, allocation and customer billing accurately reflect current network rules across markets and payment flows.

  • Protect payment cost integrity: Establish robust governance, testing and controls across scheme configurations. Reconcile expected costs against actual network charges, identify anomalies and leakage, and drive root-cause resolution.

  • Build granular visibility into payment economics: Develop robust models and analytics across markets, products, payment methods and transaction types, creating a clear view of unit economics, margin drivers and cost movements.

  • Drive structural cost and margin optimization: Identify, quantify and execute opportunities to improve economics through transaction qualification, BIN routing, cost configuration, and other levers. Partner with Product, Finance and Commercial teams to prioritize the highest-value opportunities.

  • Shape pricing and commercial decisions: Translate underlying payment economics into recommendations for customer pricing, product design, new market launches and commercial strategy, ensuring growth is supported by sustainable unit economics.

  • Build scalable infrastructure and automation: Partner with Product, Engineering, and Data teams to strengthen cost engines, fee allocation logic, dashboards and automated controls. Apply AI and advanced analytics to accelerate rule interpretation, detect anomalies and surface optimization opportunities.

  • Own complex scheme economics issues: Serve as the escalation point for scheme pricing, interchange and rule-related questions, working directly with Visa, Mastercard and other payment partners where required.

What you’ll bring

  • 7+ years of relevant experience in payments, acquiring, issuing, card networks, payment infrastructure or related roles, ideally within a global PSP, acquirer, scheme, issuer or fintech.

  • Deep knowledge of card payment economics, particularly Visa and Mastercard interchange, scheme fees, transaction qualification and network rules.

  • Strong ability to operationalize complex payment rules, translating fee schedules and network requirements into system logic, configurations and controls.

  • Experience with payment cost systems and controls, including interchange tables, scheme fee logic, BIN-based rules, transaction attributes or similar payment configurations.

  • Strong analytical and quantitative capabilities, including experience working with transaction-level data, economic modeling and reconciliation of expected versus actual payment costs.

  • Strong commercial judgment, with the ability to connect detailed payment mechanics to pricing, product decisions and margin optimization.

  • Exceptional attention to detail and ownership, with the discipline required to manage complex rules where small errors can create meaningful financial impact at scale.

  • Strong cross-functional execution, with the ability to work effectively across Product, Engineering, Finance, Data, Operations and external payment partners.

Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,700 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do. Read our operating principles to see it in full.

 

How you'll make impact

You’ll own Airwallex’s consolidated management P&L view and financial outlook, helping senior leaders understand performance, assess trade-offs and allocate resources. You’ll also be the lead finance partner to our corporate functions, including Operations, Finance, Regulatory & Compliance, Legal, People & Talent, and Communications & Government Affairs.

This is a hands-on role that combines rigorous financial planning and analysis with business partnership. You’ll work through the details, connect the implications across the business, and help leaders make informed decisions about investment, capacity and efficiency.

  • Lead consolidated planning and forecasting. Own the annual budget and quarterly forecast process, bringing together inputs across revenue, gross profit and operating expenditure. Challenge assumptions, resolve inconsistencies across plans, and ensure alignment with Airwallex’s strategic priorities, long-range plan and EBITDA targets.

  • Translate company-wide performance into decisions. Lead monthly management reporting and performance reviews, explaining the drivers of results and their implications for the outlook. Identify material risks and opportunities, build scenarios to assess trade-offs, and recommend actions to senior management.

  • Partner with corporate leaders on resource allocation. Translate business priorities into headcount and spending plans, evaluate investment requests and vendor commitments, and challenge assumptions. Help leaders prioritise resources while balancing financial discipline with capacity, service quality and control requirements.

  • Partner with People & Talent on workforce planning. Build and maintain the consolidated headcount and employee cost forecast with finance and business owners. Assess the implications of hiring pace, workforce mix and organisational changes, and keep hiring plans, budgets and forecasts aligned.

  • Drive operating leverage across corporate functions. Develop cost, capacity and productivity measures suited to each function. Evaluate opportunities through automation, process improvements and vendor arrangements, and track whether investments deliver the expected outcomes.

  • Strengthen FP&A tools, data and processes. Stay hands-on with financial models and analysis, partnering with Accounting, Data and Finance Architecture to improve reporting accuracy and planning consistency. Use AI and automation to simplify recurring work, improve forecasting and enable faster investigation of business questions.

You'll work from our London office three days a week.

What we're looking for

Essentials

  • A bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, a quantitative discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

  • 10+ years of progressive FP&A or related finance experience, with clear ownership of consolidated budgeting, forecasting, and management reporting in high-growth businesses.

  • Strong understanding of the full P&L and underlying accounting, with the ability to connect operational drivers, accruals, expense timing and one-off items to financial performance and forecast assumptions.

  • Experience partnering with corporate functions on headcount, employee costs, operating expenditure and investment decisions, including constructively challenging resource requests and assessing business cases.

  • Advanced financial modelling skills in Excel or Google Sheets, including driver-based forecasting and scenario analysis using large datasets.

  • A track record of translating complex financial analysis into clear recommendations for senior, non-finance stakeholders, with the judgement and confidence to influence decisions.

  • A hands-on approach and strong execution discipline: comfortable investigating data, resolving discrepancies and coordinating planning cycles across teams, with experience building or improving FP&A processes in a changing environment.

Preferred

  • FP&A experience in a fast-growing technology or fintech company, ideally with global exposure to SaaS, payments or multi-region business models.

  • Early-career training in Big 4 audit, deals or transaction services, investment banking, private equity or consulting, followed by in-house corporate finance experience.

  • Hands-on experience with modern FP&A or BI tools such as Pigment, Anaplan, Databricks, Tableau or Looker, and experience extracting data with SQL.

  • Practical experience applying AI or automation to financial analysis, planning or reporting workflows.

You'll thrive here if

  • You're comfortable making decisions with incomplete information and moving quickly anyway.

  • You're comfortable operating across time zones with a globally distributed team, including colleagues based in APAC and EMEA.

  • You own the outcome and you don't wait for permission to fix what's broken.

  • You connect dots across functions and hold the big picture without losing grip on the details.

  • You simplify complexity rather than hiding behind it.

Learn more about your team

Finance & Corporate Development helps Airwallex grow with control. We’re a trusted partner to the business, providing actionable insights on performance, supporting market and product expansion and helping to shape the future of our product. We ensure that Airwallex meets its financial reporting, tax and safeguarding obligations globally. We work with existing and prospective investors to raise capital and ensure it is deployed effectively.

This is a team for people who want to reimagine how the CFO office works. We’re looking for founder-like energy, high integrity and a passion for technology. You’ll thrive here if you enjoy working cross-functionally, think from first principles and can balance speed of execution with analytical precision.

About Allica Bank

Allica is the UK’s fastest growing company - and the fastest-growing financial technology (Fintech) firm ever. Our purpose is to help established SMEs, one of the last major underserved opportunities in Fintech.

Established SMEs are the backbone of local communities - representing over a third of our economy - yet have been largely neglected both by traditional high street banks and modern fintech providers.


Role Description

Our new product is a business loan for established UK SMEs, with fixed monthly repayments over 3 to 6 years. Most of the businesses we will be speaking to already know us, so the job is to reach the right people, understand what they need and take good applications from first conversation through to a funded loan.

You will be the person who owns that journey day to day: calling and emailing existing customers, running outreach campaigns, collecting the information we need to underwrite, and keeping the pipeline accurate so the team can see what is working. You will work closely with Risk, Legal and Data, and report progress to senior leadership each week.

Principal Accountabilities

  • Make outbound calls to existing and previous customers, hold clear discovery conversations about what they need the funding for, and record every outcome in HubSpot

  • Maintain a consistent follow up routine

  • Collect bank statements or Open Banking connections and any other documents needed, and pass complete applications to Underwriting with the context they need

  • Explain loan terms, pricing, arrangement fees and personal guarantees clearly and accurately, and know when to hand a question to Risk or Compliance rather than answer it yourself

  • Support customers through offer, KYC refresh, legal documents and direct debit set up until the loan is funded

  • Treat declines and customers who are not interested with care, and refer customers elsewhere only with their consent

  • Run outreach campaigns across email, statement emails, SMS, Whatsapp and LinkedIn, working with the Data team on audiences and reviewing the results

  • Keep the CRM up to date, tidy and consistent, including the reason for every rejection or decision not to proceed

  • Provide weekly reports on calls made, conversations held, applications, offers and funded loans, and flag what is and isn't working

  • Work closely with Risk, Legal and Data to keep applications moving and customers well served

  • Comply with all mandatory policies and adhere to operational procedures to maintain internal controls

Personal Attributes & Experience

  • 1-3 years of experience in a commercial business development or relationship role, ideally in lending, finance or fintech

  • Confident and credible on the phone with small business owners and directors, and comfortable making a high volume of calls

  • Clear, accurate written communication, and the discipline to follow up and keep records up to date

  • Strong numerical ability, with the confidence to work with loan amounts, interest rates, terms, repayments and fees

  • Organised, self-directed and able to manage a busy pipeline of customers at different stages

  • Honest and careful about what can and cannot be promised to a customer, in a regulated environment

  • Knowledge of SME lending, including unsecured loans, personal guarantees or government-backed schemes

  • Experience with a CRM such as HubSpot, and with email or SMS campaign tools

  • Familiarity with Open Banking, KYC and credit underwriting processes

  • Experience of working with brokers or introducers

raw.description:
About Artificial

Help shape the future of specialty insurance

At Artificial, we’re building the next generation of technology for the specialty (re)insurance market. Our mission is to transform how brokers and carriers operate in complex markets by removing operational barriers and enabling smarter, faster decision-making.

We use modern technology to solve real challenges for some of the world’s leading brokers and insurers. By automating the repetitive and structuring the complex, we help our partners unlock new opportunities for innovation and growth.

You’ll be joining a collaborative team that values curiosity, ownership, and continuous learning. We work in an environment where ideas are heard, support is built-in, and outcomes matter. Everyone here has the chance to make a tangible impact on our products, our customers, and the industry.

We've just raised $45M (£33M) in Series B funding from lead investor CommerzVentures, new investor Move Capital, as well as all existing shareholders. This investment round gives us the room to grow with confidence, continue to innovate, and ensure that Artificial remains the first choice for brokers and carriers seeking a smarter way to trade digitally.

Join us, and take the chance to be a part of something that will change the landscape of insurance for generations.

About the role

At Artificial, there are three primary sources of documentation we maintain:

  1. Client-facing product documentation for insurance business users (brokers, underwriters and operations teams using our platform)

  2. Our internal documentation site, which is our most heavily used documentation surface, built docs-as-code from the engineering repository and authored largely by engineers.

  3. Our public API documentation, owned and authored by our Integrations team from auto-generated OpenAPI specifications.

The below responsibilities break down how each of these three sources are to be managed.

Responsibilities

  • Own the client-facing product documentation (1) end-to-end: strategy, information architecture, standards, tooling and content quality

  • Own the internal documentation gap backlog (2):

    • proactively identify potential gaps and triage incoming gap reports

    • route each one to the best-placed author and chase it to completion

    • write the content yourself where you're the right author

  • Steward the internal documentation site (2) and public API documentation (3): set the standards, information architecture and editorial bar for content authored by engineering and integrations teams, and keep the publishing pipelines healthy

  • Interview engineers about new features as they ship, and demystify them for non-technical readers before anyone has to ask

  • Act as editorial reviewer on documentation changes, catching duplication, misplacement and unclear writing before it ships

  • Write and maintain the highest-value client-facing content yourself: core product guides and release communications

  • Select, build and run the documentation toolchain, including docs-as-code workflows (static site generators, CI/CD, review gates) where they serve us best

  • Design and operate AI-assisted authoring pipelines that raise quality and throughput without sacrificing accuracy

  • Build the contribution model: templates, style standards and review processes that let product managers and engineers contribute content you curate rather than gatekeep

  • Partner with the Integrations team on API documentation: raise the quality of guides and examples around the auto-generated reference without taking authorship away from the experts

  • Partner with product and customer-facing teams so documentation ships with releases, not after them

  • Measure whether documentation is working: usage, search behaviour, support deflection and client feedback, and act on what you find

  • Set the standard for clear technical communication across the company

About you

  • 6+ years in technical writing, documentation engineering or a closely related discipline

  • Preferably an ex Engineer who has stepped into technical writing / documentation

  • Demonstrable experience producing end-user product documentation, plus enough developer documentation experience to edit and improve API guides credibly

  • Hands-on experience owning documentation tooling, including docs-as-code workflows (for example Git-based authoring, static site generators, CI pipelines)

  • A portfolio or writing samples that show you can make complex technical material clear for both technical and non-technical readers

  • Used to working in a fast-paced, technological environment, with all the ambiguities this presents: flexibility will be needed

  • Confident in reading and understanding code and pull requests, so that you are able to identify where documentation might need adding/editing

We especially want to hear from you if you have:

  • Built or substantially restructured a documentation estate, not just contributed to one

  • Experience establishing contribution models where engineers and product managers write and you edit and curate

  • Practical experience using LLMs in documentation workflows, with a clear-eyed view of where they help and where they fail

  • Familiarity with structured documentation frameworks such as Diataxis

  • Familiarity with OpenAPI specifications and generating reference documentation from source

About Artificial

Help shape the future of specialty insurance

At Artificial, we’re building the next generation of technology for the specialty (re)insurance market. Our mission is to transform how brokers and carriers operate in complex markets by removing operational barriers and enabling smarter, faster decision-making.

You’ll be joining a collaborative team that values curiosity, ownership, and continuous learning. We work in an environment where ideas are heard, support is built-in, and outcomes matter. Everyone here has the chance to make a tangible impact on our products, our customers, and the industry.

We've just raised $45M (£33M) in Series B funding from lead investor CommerzVentures, new investor Move Capital, as well as all existing shareholders. This investment round gives us the room to grow with confidence, continue to innovate, and ensure that Artificial remains the first choice for brokers and carriers seeking a smarter way to trade digitally.

Join us, and take the chance to be a part of something that will change the landscape of insurance for generations.

About the role

Today, a key part of delivery has no clear owner: problem framing before configuration begins.

  • On the customer side, there are rarely UX specialists - only domain experts and sponsors who describe needs as pre-formed solutions.

  • On our side, configured workspaces are built by Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) in our Transform team: experts in the platform, accountable for shipping to a deadline, but not trained designers.

  • Our Platform teams have design expertise but are often too far removed from individual implementations to influence the moments that matter most.

The result is pretty predictable: we move quickly into “how” before we are confident about the “what” and “why.”

Your mandate is to slow down at the right moment and make sure we’re solving the right problem - then help the team implement the best platform-valid solution.

This is a founding role. You would be the first Forward Deployed Designer (FDD) at Artificial, hired into an enabling function within the Platform team, with the mandate to define how the function works and to build it out. Later, FDDs would join the Transform teams in hands-on client roles: you’d take part in hiring them (with our support), then line-manage them directly.

Responsibilities

You would work closely with the Transform team and customers throughout discovery and delivery. In practice, that means:

  • Establish the FDD function. Define the operating model, the patterns, and the ways of working from scratch.

  • Grow and manage the team. Take part in hiring subsequent FDDs and line-manage them as they join.

  • Join customer + FDE sessions early (problem framing and discovery), not only at reviews once decisions are already fixed.

  • Translate requests into problems. For example, turn “we need a confirmation button before this step” into:

    • the user behaviour driving the request

    • two or three platform-valid approaches

    • a recommendation, with trade-offs explained

  • Prototype and test ideas quickly using the most effective medium (written specs, wireframes, workflows, or light code). We care more about clarity and platform realism than polished artefacts.

  • Provide credible pushback when the customer’s proposed solution doesn’t address the underlying problem.

  • Codify patterns and precedents so knowledge moves from individual memory into shared team infrastructure.

  • Level up the FDE team’s design instincts over time. You shouldn’t be the only person who can think about UX across the two teams; part of the job is coaching, so the capability can spread.

  • Use workspace signals (e.g. session data and call analysis) to surface risks early - before they become escalations.

About you

You are a designer who thrives in ambiguity and constraints, someone who can bring structure, judgement, and clarity to complex, real-world delivery.

You likely have experience in enterprise/B2B software where:

  • the design system already exists

  • the hard part is framing the right problem and navigating stakeholders

  • solutions must work within meaningful technical and organisational constraints

You understand technical concepts fluently. Part of the role would involve writing code (with plenty of LLM and human assistance) using our in-house DSL (Domain Specific Language). We don’t want you to be an engineer, but we do need you to be comfortable reading and writing some code, reasoning about how a configurable system behaves, and understanding what the platform can and can’t express, well enough to hold a credible conversation with engineers and to explain these constraints to customers when necessary.

You have managed designers. You’re comfortable with line management of a small team (roughly three to five people) and have hired designers before. Early on, you’d do this hands-on yourself; as the function grows, you’d manage the FDDs who follow.

Insurance or Lloyd’s experience is a plus, but is not a requirement. We care more about how you think about complex platforms and stakeholders than about prior domain knowledge, which you can learn here.

We especially want to hear from you if you have

  • Collaborative skills with an emphasis on product quality.

  • Experience in insurtech, insurance or related industries.

  • Strong problem-solving skills.

  • Experience in a distributed work environment.

offer.title: Senior Research Scientist, AI Safety and Biosecurity

raw.title: Senior Research Scientist, AI Safety and Biosecurity
raw.description:
About Us

Basecamp Research is building frontier AI for therapeutic design. We believe the future of medicine lies in reprogramming the body to repair itself, and we design the models and the medicines to teach it how.

Our EDEN models are trained on BaseData, the world's largest proprietary genomic dataset, with over 10B genes collected through partnerships in more than 30 countries across all seven continents. This gives our AI models access to genetic diversity that doesn't exist in public databases, and enables EDEN to design cell and gene therapies, enzymes, and peptides directly from information about a disease. Our pipeline of EDEN-designed therapeutics, beginning with in vivo cell therapy, is advancing towards clinical development.

In September 2026 we closed an oversubscribed $140M Series C led by S32, with participation from NVIDIA, Anthropic's Anthology Fund, Catalio, European Tech Collective, Firebrand River Capital, King Philanthropies, NATO Innovation Fund, NVentures (NVIDIA's venture arm), Redalpine, Rockefeller Foundation, Singular, Sovereign AI and True Ventures. We have offices and labs in London and Boston, we partner with biopharma companies and academic institutions worldwide, and our work has been recognised by Fast Company's Top 10 Most Innovative Companies in Biotech, the FT-backed Sifted AI100 list of Europe's leading AI startups as well as Barclays Eagle Labs Ones to watch, AI100.

At Basecamp Research, we pride ourselves on being a lean collaborative and global team with extremely specialist and unique skills. Our biologists, engineers, ML scientists and field explorers are united by a sense of adventure and the belief that AI, biology and data, will result in new medicines for patients who have few options today.

The Role

You will advance our work on AI safety and biosecurity, studying the capabilities and risks of biological AI systems and developing methods to evaluate them and make them safer.

We train frontier biological models on BaseData, which captures genetic diversity beyond what is available in public databases. You will work within the team that develops these models, with access to the data, training process, and biological expertise needed to study their capabilities and test safeguards.

You will build on our existing safety work and help set research priorities as our models develop. Depending on your expertise, your work could include:

  • Designing evaluations and red-teaming studies that measure what biological AI systems enable in practice, including how much they add to existing tools and expertise.

  • Developing threat models grounded in biology, and working with experimental scientists to establish when computational results support conclusions about real-world capabilities or risk.

  • Investigating model behaviour, representations, and generalisation to understand where safety evaluations and safeguards hold up or fail.

  • Developing and testing safeguards across training, model behaviour, design screening, and access, measuring both their effectiveness and their effect on useful scientific work.

We will shape the research focus together around your strengths and the problems that matter most. You will lead projects from the initial question through to experiments and methods that the team can use. Your findings will inform how we develop our models and what we publish, release, and offer through our services. You will also have scope to publish research where appropriate and collaborate with the wider AI safety and biosecurity community.

You will report to the Head of AI Research and work alongside researchers in genomics, sequence modelling, and large-scale deep learning, as well as computational biologists and

experimental teams across the company.

About You

You have a strong record of original research in machine learning, AI safety, computational biology, biosecurity, or a closely related field. We want to see work that has advanced understanding or changed research practice: influential papers, research tools used by others, evaluations adopted by other teams, or methods that changed how a system was built or deployed.

You bring deep expertise in a relevant area, such as model evaluation, interpretability, robustness, safeguards, biological modelling, or quantitative assessment of biological risk. You understand modern machine learning and can write the code, run the experiments, and analyse the results needed to test your ideas.

You have a PhD in a relevant field or an equivalent research record, and have led substantial research projects. You can explain your own contribution, the choices you made, and what you learned when an approach did not work.

You are curious about biology and willing to learn its details, whether you already work on biological AI or bring methods from another domain. You work closely with domain experts and recognise when a model score is insufficient evidence for a biological claim.

You exercise good judgement under uncertainty. You design experiments with appropriate controls, look for alternative explanations, and communicate findings and limitations clearly enough for others to act on them.

You work well in a small research team: sharing credit, taking criticism seriously, and helping colleagues solve problems outside your immediate project. You care about enabling useful scientific and medical applications of AI and are motivated to make them safer.

Nice to Have

  • Research experience in AI safety or biosecurity, including evaluations, red-teaming, or threat modelling.

  • Experience with protein design, genomic models, structure prediction, or other biological AI systems.

  • Experimental biology experience, or computational research validated in collaboration with an experimental team.

  • Experience implementing and evaluating safeguards in deployed systems.

  • Collaboration with biosecurity organisations, synthesis screening initiatives, or AI safety institutes.

Compensation and benefits

What we offer in return

  • Impactful Mission: This is a rare chance to do work that genuinely matters. You'll join a talented, fast-moving team, access unique biological datasets at scale, and see your contributions shape real breakthroughs in AI and curative therapeutics..

  • Collaborative Culture: You'll be surrounded by world-class engineers, scientists, and researchers who care deeply about their work and about each other. With offices in London and Boston, we've built a flexible, cross-functional environment where personal development and real ownership aren't just talking points.

  • High Growth: We truly believe in investing our people we make coaching available to team members during steep growth journeys and we have twice yearly promotion opportunities. People who are really successful here own it and go directly to solve problems at pace and we ensure reward increases with impact.

  • Comprehensive Benefits: We've built a benefits package people value. That means competitive salary, equity, and private healthcare with no medical history exclusions so strong that means most employees' family members opt into our plan over their own. We also offer Carrot Fertility with IVF stipend, salary sacrifice pension, bike to work scheme, life insurance, and more.

We are committed to equal opportunity employment regardless of ethnic or national origin, race, religion, sex, age, citizenship, sexual orientation, marital status, disability, gender identity or any other basis. If you have a disability or additional need that needs accommodating do let us know.

raw.title: Marketing Manager
raw.description:
BeyondMath is a pioneering startup, backed by top-tier VCs, on a mission to reshape the frontiers of engineering through Foundational AI models for Physics. We are replacing traditional, slow, and expensive simulation methods with AI that rivals accuracy at orders of magnitude higher speed.

We are moving beyond the "generic AI" hype to solve the world's hardest physical engineering challenges in automotive, consumer electronics, aerospace, and energy. We are looking for a Marketing Manager to be our first dedicated marketing hire: a hands-on operator who will build and run the channels, materials and events that put our technology in front of the engineers who need it.

The Role

As Marketing Manager, you are the person who makes BeyondMath's marketing actually happen. This is an execution role, not a strategy role: you will report to our GTM Lead, who sets direction with the CEO and COO, and you own turning it into a steady, high-quality stream of output across our social channels, our go-to-market materials and our events calendar.

You will work closely with the leadership team, our GTM and technical account teams, and our engineers and researchers, turning deeply technical work with global OEMs, Formula 1 teams and aerospace innovators into content and moments the market notices. You will not inherit a marketing machine; you will build one, with real autonomy, a direct line to leadership, and the BeyondMath brand system already in place to work from.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own Our Social Channels: Run BeyondMath's LinkedIn and other relevant channels day to day — content calendar, copy, visuals, scheduling, community engagement and reporting — with a consistent voice and an on-brand look.

  • Content Production: Turn product releases, customer results, research and team news into posts, short articles, case studies, one-pagers and short-form video, working directly with engineers and researchers to get the technical detail right.

  • GTM Materials & Preparation: Support the GTM team with decks, one-pagers, proposals, demo collateral and follow-up materials, and maintain a current library of on-brand templates they can pick up and use.

  • Events Calendar & Attendance: Own the events calendar across industry conferences, partner events and executive dinners or roundtables. Plan BeyondMath's presence end to end: selection and budget, sponsorships, speaker slots, booth and materials, logistics, attendee outreach, onsite execution and post-event follow-up and reporting.

  • Owned Events & Webinars: Produce BeyondMath-hosted moments — technical webinars, customer roundtables, launch events — from concept through follow-up.

  • Website, Email & Digital: Keep website content current (news, case studies, careers), look after basic SEO hygiene, and run newsletter and email communications to prospects and partners.

  • Brand Guardianship: Apply and maintain the BeyondMath brand guidelines across all internal and external materials, and brief and manage freelancers or agencies (design, video, PR) where needed.

  • Measurement: Track channel, content and event performance, report simply on what is working, and keep marketing data in the CRM clean and usable for the GTM team.

About You

  • You have a "founder's mentality": you are a builder who is comfortable being the first person in a function, and who will set up the system and then run it yourself.

  • You take pride in output. You would rather ship ten strong posts and two excellent events than write one strategy deck.

  • You are at home with deeply technical subject matter and genuinely curious about engineering, simulation and AI. You do not need to be an engineer, but you need to enjoy working with them.

  • You are organised, detail-obsessed and reliable across many concurrent deadlines, and you bring a calm, can-do attitude to a fast-moving team.

Essential Requirements

  • Experience: 3–7 years' B2B marketing experience, ideally in a startup or scale-up and ideally in technology, software, engineering or deep tech.

  • Social Channel Ownership: A hands-on track record running company social channels, LinkedIn in particular — content calendars, copywriting, visuals, community management and analytics.

  • Events Delivery: Proven experience planning and delivering B2B events and conference attendance end to end, including sponsorships, logistics and onsite execution.

  • Writing: Strong writing and editing. You produce clean, accurate copy quickly and can work with engineers to make complex things clear without dumbing them down.

  • Tooling: Working proficiency in presentation and design tools (PowerPoint or Google Slides, Canva or Figma) and everyday marketing tooling (CRM and email, social scheduling, web analytics).

  • AI-Native: Fluent, daily use of AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT or similar) across your marketing workflow.

  • Travel: Willing and able to travel for events across the UK and Europe, with occasional travel further afield.

Highly Desirable

  • Technical Audiences: Experience marketing to engineering, manufacturing or industrial audiences (automotive, aerospace, energy, motorsport), or within CAE, simulation or engineering software.

  • First Marketer: Experience as the sole or first marketing hire in a company.

  • Video: Short-form video production and editing for social.

  • CRM & Web: Working knowledge of a B2B CRM and a website CMS.

  • PR: Experience with press, media relations and announcements.

Why Join Us?

  • Full Ownership: You will own how BeyondMath shows up in the market — our channels, our materials and our events — and build the marketing function from the ground up.

  • High Impact: Your work puts our technology in front of the engineers designing the next generation of sustainable transport and energy systems.

  • Elite Team: Work alongside veterans from world-leading AI labs and top-tier engineering teams in a culture of "impact with integrity."

raw.description:
About Brillio:

Brillio is one of the fastest growing digital technology service providers and a partner of choice for many Fortune 1000 companies seeking to turn disruption into a competitive advantage through innovative digital adoption. Brillio, renowned for its world-class professionals, referred to as "Brillians", distinguishes itself through their capacity to seamlessly integrate cutting-edge digital and design thinking skills with an unwavering dedication to client satisfaction.
Brillio takes pride in its status as an employer of choice, consistently attracting the most exceptional and talented individuals due to its unwavering emphasis on contemporary, groundbreaking technologies, and exclusive digital projects. Brillio's relentless commitment to providing an exceptional experience to its Brillians and nurturing their full potential consistently garners them the Great Place to Work® certification year after year.

We are seeking a high-energy, net new Sales Director to drive growth for our ServiceNow advisory, implementation, and managed services business in the UK. The ideal candidate will have a strong network within the ServiceNow ecosystem and a proven track record of selling ITSM, ITOM, ITAM, and related ServiceNow propositions into enterprise clients.

Responsibilities
  • Identify, prospect, and close new enterprise accounts for ServiceNow services in the UK market.
  • Build and leverage relationships with ServiceNow sales, alliances, and partner teams.
  • Position our advisory, implementation, and managed services portfolio to align with client business needs.
  • Manage the full sales cycle from lead generation through contract negotiation and closure.
  • Work in close collaboration with Brillio’s presales team & practice teams to ensure that proposed offerings and services fully meet customers’ business and technology needs.
  • Demonstrate strong personal communication and presentation skills to establish interest, credibility, and trust.

    • Qualifications
  • 7-10+ years of enterprise sales experience, with at least 3 years selling ServiceNow services. 
  • Proven track record of quota attainment with mid-tier or new-age IT services providers.
  • Deep understanding of ServiceNow ecosystem (partners, alliances, go-to-market motions).
  • Strong track record of net-new business acquisition in the UK market.
  • Excellent relationship building, consultative selling, and negotiation skills. 
  • Strong understanding of the business challenges associated within enterprise customers and how ServiceNow helps solve them
  • Strong understanding of the possibilities of ServiceNow and how it integrates and associates itself to other toolsets 
  • Appreciation of surrounding toolsets and competing platforms, and the benefits of ServiceNow over these surrounding and competing toolsets
  • Ability to operate independently with a hunter’s mindset and entrepreneurial drive.

    • Critical Leadership Qualities
  • Customer Advocacy - Ensures customer success on stated and unstated business priorities through strategic advice and market leading solutions.
  • Owner’s Mindset - Is passionate about Brillio’s business, deeply committed to its success and makes decisions that are in the best interest of the firm.
  • Innovation Ethos - Embraces ambiguity and adopts relentless experimentation to challenge current practices and enable continuous growth.
  • Execution with Pace - Displays agility to deliver high quality results in the face of changing stakeholder expectations.
  • Big Picture Thinking - Creates a common definition of shared success and sets bold targets that inspire the team towards new horizons.
  • Winning Through Teams - Enables a culture of collaboration and empowers teams to "raise their game” in order to create a winning formula.

raw.description:
OUR MISSION

To become the car-changing destination of choice. By combining technology, media and deep automotive expertise, we've turned how people buy, sell, advertise and lease cars on its head.

What started as a simple reviews site is now one of the largest online car-changing destinations in Europe. Last year alone we grew over 50% with nearly £3bn worth of cars bought on site, while £1.8bn of cars were listed for sale through our Sell My Car service.

In 2024 we went big and acquired Autovia - creators of AutoExpress and Evo magazines - doubling our audience overnight. Together we now have one of the biggest YouTube channels in the world with almost 10m subscribers and over 1.1 billion annual views, while we sell 1.2 million print copies of our magazines and have an annual web content reach over 350million.

And we’re a long way from done!

Carwow is hiring for a Account Manager to join our Get Your Car (New Market) team, focused on car buying.

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

  • Become an expert on your brands, gaining a deep understanding of their challenges, opportunities and overall performance on the Carwow platform.

  • Maintain regular and proactive communication with clients, primarily through phone and video calls, to build strong and long lasting relationships.

  • Provide insightful performance analysis and recommend process improvements to dealer partners to enhance their return on investment on Carwow.

  • Lead the onboarding and training of new dealerships, ensuring a seamless experience and driving high retention rates.

  • Take ownership of your portfolio’s performance, with clear targets including the upselling of additional products and services.

THE ROLE

Buying and selling a car should feel like one seamless motion for a dealer, not two separate systems. Right now it's the opposite: a dealer buys through us, then has to manage collection, payment and resale largely on their own, stitching together workflows across multiple platforms and channels, much of it manual.

For a dealer, speed is money. Every extra day a car sits before it's collected, priced, and paid for is a day of depreciation, tied-up capital, and a missed chance to buy the next one.If we can get a dealer from 'I've bought this car' to 'it's ready and paid for' faster through transport and collections, quicker final pricing, and Wallet, we make them more profitable. A dealer who's more profitable because of Carwow has little reason to go elsewhere: they'll lean on us more, and churn less.

This role owns that last-mile agenda: getting cars collected quickly, resolving final price without friction, and making Wallet work the way dealers expect it to. This team sits across our ambitions to make car changing a seamless journey, this role's job is the handover itself: the operational moment between buying and being ready to sell again. This is also a moment where AI changes what's possible. Dealers are already asking for smarter scheduling, less manual chasing, and tools that reduce the overhead of running a business. We want to build those things. The PM in this role will need the curiosity to explore what that could look like, and the rigour to distinguish genuine value from noise. If you want to own an operational product area end to end, work with some of the most sophisticated buyers in UK retail, and build things that have a direct line to commercial outcomes, this is it.

raw.description:
OUR MISSION

To become the car-changing destination of choice. By combining technology, media and deep automotive expertise, we've turned how people buy, sell, advertise and lease cars on its head.

What started as a simple reviews site is now one of the largest online car-changing destinations in Europe. Last year alone we grew over 50% with nearly £3bn worth of cars bought on site, while £1.8bn of cars were listed for sale through our Sell My Car service.

In 2024 we went big and acquired Autovia - creators of AutoExpress and Evo magazines - doubling our audience overnight. Together we now have one of the biggest YouTube channels in the world with almost 10m subscribers and over 1.1 billion annual views, while we sell 1.2 million print copies of our magazines and have an annual web content reach over 350million.

And we’re a long way from done!

THE ROLE

The Transactional Financial Controller owns the full Accounts Payable, Billing function, Credit control, working capital management, and banking operations across the group, while also leading the ongoing automation and optimisation of the finance systems that underpin transactional finance. This is a hybrid role based in London combining hands-on operational leadership of AP, Billing and credit control teams and processes with responsibility for driving system-led improvement, control, and efficiency across the wider finance systems landscape along with the Finance transformation team.This role has line management responsibility for a team based in London and Porto, working under hybrid and remote arrangements

 

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

Transactional Finance (AP, Billing and Credit control) Management

  • Full management of the Accounts Payable and Billing and Credit control functions, including team leadership, prioritisation and quality control.

  • Oversight of all banking and expense transactions, ensuring accuracy, timeliness and appropriate controls.

  • Own working capital management, including planning and execution of payment runs.

  • Implement and manage the Purchase Order (PO) system end-to-end, liaising with stakeholders across the business to ensure compliance and efficient processing.

raw.title: Embedded Software Engineer (LDN)
raw.description:
For over four decades, Cirrus Logic has been propelled by the top engineers in mixed-signal processing. Our rockstar team thrives on solving complex challenges with innovative end-user solutions for the world's top consumer brands. Cirrus Logic is also known for its award-winning culture, built on a foundation of inclusion and fairness, meaningful community engagement, and delivering enjoyable employee experiences at every turn. But we couldn’t do it without our extraordinary workforce – and that’s where you come in. Join our team and help us continue to make Cirrus Logic an exceptional place to grow your career! 

We’re looking for an Embedded Software Engineer who thrives close to the hardware and enjoys building high-performance, reliable firmware for DSP architecture and microcontrollers (e.g., RISC V and Arm Cortex M/A). You’ll design and implement real-time embedded software, optimize compute-heavy pipelines, and collaborate with hardware and systems teams to bring products from concept to production.
 
This role suits someone who can move comfortably between architecture/design, low-level firmware, and performance tuning—especially where latency, throughput, power, and determinism matter.

Key Responsibilities:
  • Design, implement, and maintain embedded firmware for DSP cores and MCUs (RISC V and/or Arm).
  • Build and optimize real-time signal-processing pipelines (fixed-point and/or floating-point), potentially including FFTs, filters, modulation/demodulation, codecs, feature extraction, or control loops.
  • Develop firmware using a mix of C/C++ (and selective assembly where appropriate), with strong focus on performance, memory, and power optimization.
  • Work with SoC/board peripherals: DMA, timers, SPI, I²C, UART, I²S/TDM, PWM, GPIO, and relevant bus fabrics.
  • Bring up new hardware: boot flows, clocks, memory maps, interrupt vectors, peripheral init, and early validation.
  • Implement and debug drivers and RTOS components (e.g., Zephyr or equivalent), including task scheduling, synchronization primitives, and ISR design.
  • Develop test strategies: unit tests, hardware-in-the-loop tests, test automation, and manufacturing/production diagnostics.
  • Use debugging/profiling tools: JTAG/SWD, logic analyzers, oscilloscopes, trace (ETM/ITM), and cycle-accurate profiling when available.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with hardware, FPGA/ASIC, systems, and application teams to define requirements and interfaces.
  • Contribute documentation: architecture notes, interface specs, timing budgets, work packages, and bring-up guides.
  • Participate in code reviews and help establish best practices for embedded quality, safety, and maintainability.

    • Required Skills and Qualifications:
  • Strong professional experience developing embedded firmware in C/C++ for MCUs and/or DSPs.
  • Hands-on experience with RISC V and/or Arm architecture (Cortex M/A), including interrupts, memory, caches, and performance characteristics.
  • Solid understanding of embedded software fundamentals:
  • register-level programming, memory-mapped I/O
  • concurrency (ISRs, RTOS tasks), race conditions, timing determinism
  • fixed-point arithmetic, numerical precision, and overflow/underflow management
  • Proven ability to optimize firmware: cycle counting, memory layout, DMA usage, cache behavior, minimizing latency and jitter.
  • Comfortable with toolchains and build systems:
  • GCC/LLVM-based toolchains, cross-compilation
  • CMake/Make, Meson, linker scripts, map files
  • Strong debugging skills with hardware and firmware:
  • JTAG/SWD debugging
  • root-cause analysis of timing and performance issues
  • Source control expertise (Git) and disciplined engineering practices (code reviews, CI).

    • Preferred Skills and Qualifications:
  • Languages: C, C++, (optional) assembly, Python for test tooling/scripts
  • Architectures: RISC V, Arm Cortex M/A, DSP cores
  • RTOS/OS: Zephyr, embedded Linux (optional)
  • Tools: JTAG/SWD debuggers, GDB, OpenOCD/J-Link, logic analyzer, oscilloscope, trace tools
  • Practices: profiling, timing analysis, unit/integration testing, CI/CD for embedded
  • Experience with common DSP libraries/techniques (e.g., CMSIS-DSP, vendor DSP libs) and SIMD/vector optimization patterns.
  • Experience with Zephyr, or embedded Linux on Arm.
  • Familiarity with bootloaders, secure boot, OTA update mechanisms, and field diagnostics.
  • Understanding of digital communications, or audio, processing domains.
  • Exposure to safety/security standards (e.g., MISRA C/C++, IEC 61508, ISO 26262)
    • This Newbury or London based role is a hybrid remote position and will follow a 2 day in-office work schedule, with in-office days based on business needs and team preference. You must be based within commutable distance of the work location listed on the job posting, or willing to relocate prior to beginning employment with Cirrus Logic.

raw.title: Account Executive (GTME - Enterprise)
raw.description:
About Clay

AI is unleashing the biggest wave of company creation in history. Clay's mission is to be the engine those companies use to grow to their full potential.

Clay predicts the next best action for your business and then helps you take it. We started by aggregating the best data for B2B companies. Then, we built the infrastructure to run any personalized campaign on top of it, including emails, ads, landing pages, and workflows that make reps more productive. Now, we're building agents that can help grow your company for you. We're already helping thousands of customers — including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and Visa — go to market with unique data, signals, and AI research.

In 2026, we raised a $115M Series D at $7.1B Valuation led by Wellington — and are on track to cross $200M in revenue this quarter. We also launched a $1M Scholarship fund for GTME Education.

Some things to know about us:

  • Our community includes 17,000+ customers, 200+ integration partners, 125+ agencies, 50+ Clay clubs, and 30k members on Slack.

  • Our culture is unique inside and outside of work. Our team members are also DJs, activists, writers, clowns, marathoners, skydivers, psychedelic therapists, social workers, and more.

  • All employees can work with world-class coaches who specialize in creativity, management, and more.

  • Our operating principles — including negative maintenance and non-attached action — guide our work. Read more about them here.

  • Read about us in the NYT, Forbes, First Round Review, and more.

Hear from our employees directly on our Glassdoor page!

GTM Engineer @ Clay

Clay is the GTM platform of choice for the best revenue teams in the world. From Anthropic to Notion to Stripe, growth teams use Clay to find their GTM Alpha. Our journey to $100M ARR was powered by creativity and a belief that the best GTM teams treat their go-to-market like a product: constantly shipping new plays, experimenting, and never assuming that what worked last quarter will work next quarter. We sell that way too.

We describe ourselves as go-to-market consultants: AEs with a product mindset. We don't just sell Clay. We learn how a prospect's GTM motion actually works and show them what's possible with Clay. Every deal is a net-new customer discovering Clay for the first time. Our motion is high-velocity but consultative; we move fast, but we also go deep. This role won't look the same in six months as it does today, and that's the point. We're looking for people who want to grow alongside us and help redefine what great selling looks like.

What You'll Do

  • Own and close net-new business end-to-end

  • Prospect into target accounts and build pipeline alongside managing inbound leads

  • Run tailored product evaluations and demos that connect Clay's capabilities to a prospect's specific workflows and pain points

  • Lead consultative discovery that helps prospects see the possibilities of Clay

  • Build business cases that win budget and internal champions

  • Work cross-functionally with product, engineering, services, and customer teams to shape solutions and stay sharp on what Clay can do

  • Help build our sales playbook, processes, and culture as we scale

  • Use AI creatively, whether to improve your workflows or those of your customers

What You'll Bring

  • 5+ years in a closing role (AE, senior AE, or sales leader) with a track record of carrying and exceeding quota in an Enterprise or Strategic sales motion

  • Proven ability to build pipeline, not just manage it

  • Experience closing mid-market new-logo deals with multiple stakeholders in a consultative, solutions-oriented selling motion

  • High business IQ: you can walk into a conversation with a company you've never sold to, quickly understand their GTM motion, and identify where Clay creates value. This is the single most important skill in the role

  • Creative and resourceful, whether that's finding clever ways to use AI tools in your own work or learning and pitching all of Clay’s exciting use cases

  • Experience with a formal sales methodology (we don't care which one, but you have a structured approach to running deals)

  • You're a strong communicator who can hold a room without dominating it

  • You're excited about contributing to a growing team, not just hitting your own number

Why This Role

The best GTM teams we work with don't run the same playbook forever. They ship new plays constantly, automate what's manual, and treat every part of their go-to-market as something that can be improved. We do the same internally, and as a GTME, you'll be immersed in that culture and bring those ideas directly into how you sell.

We believe we're building the future of what great salespeople look like in a post-AI world. You'll get a front-row seat to how the best GTM teams in tech actually operate, across every motion, segment, and vertical. You'll build relationships with revenue leaders at companies you admire and develop the pattern recognition that makes great GTM leaders.

If you don't fit the mold of a traditional account executive, you're welcome here. People from non-traditional backgrounds (founders, software engineers, former educators, product managers, and more!) have shaped our sales organization in meaningful ways.

Meet our amazing GTME crew!
