Our AI solutions enhance efficiency, spark creativity, and drive insightful decision-making, empowering our teams to produce innovative and impactful results. 

Role: Regional Operations Director (EMEA)

Location: London, United Kingdom (3 days a week from our London offices)

About the role: 

The Regional Operations Director is accountable for the operational effectiveness of the EMEA region. Reporting to the Global Chief Transformation and Operations Officer, you'll translate the global operating model into practical, market-specific execution — building the structure, governance and performance focus needed to strengthen operational control and support scalable growth.

You'll lead a regional operations team, partner closely with regional and global leadership, and act as the key connector between regional execution and global capability. The role calls for a leader equally comfortable setting strategic direction and solving complex operational problems hands-on — someone who turns data into action, builds high-performing teams, and keeps commercial performance firmly in focus.

What you will be doing: 

 

Regional operational leadership

  • Set clear priorities, accountabilities and ways of working for the EMEA Regional Operations function.
  • Build the structure, rhythm and capability needed to improve client delivery, business performance and regional growth.
  • Act as the senior operational partner to Regional Leadership on risks, performance, capacity and improvement priorities.

Client delivery operations

  • Own the operational run model for EMEA clients — including cadence, governance, issue resolution and escalation management.
  • Partner with Account Leadership to ensure delivery risks are visible, blockers are resolved quickly and client teams are set up to deliver effectively.
  • Ensure regional clients are mobilised and supported through consistent operating standards and reliable delivery controls.

Governance, cadence and decision management

  • Own the regional governance rhythm: forums, communications, decision-making and performance reviews.
  • Ensure decisions are made at the right level, escalations are routed effectively and regional context is represented in relevant global and regional forums.
  • Drive clear actions, accountability and follow-through across the function.

Operating model execution

  • Embed the global operating model across EMEA, ensuring standards, processes, tools and governance expectations are adopted consistently.
  • Translate enterprise-level standards into practical, market-specific ways of working.

Resource and capacity management

  • Own the regional view of demand, supply, utilisation, resource mix and capacity gaps.
  • Partner with Global Capacity Management, Account Teams, Delivery Leads and Offshore Operations to optimise deployment, resolve constraints and improve utilisation.
  • Provide regional input into enterprise workforce planning and future capacity needs.

Business and client enablement

  • Ensure regional client teams have the operational foundations needed to mobilise and deliver work effectively.
  • Coordinate core business processes including client onboarding, timesheeting, billing readiness, interagency set-ups, compliance and headcount approvals.
  • Act as the regional operational point of coordination for enablement issues, working across Finance, HR, Technology and Implementation to unblock dependencies.

Commercial performance and margin management

  • Manage the operational levers that affect cost-to-serve across the region, including scope leakage, resource efficiency, rework and avoidable cost.
  • Partner with Account Leadership and Finance to improve margin visibility and ensure practical actions are in place to protect profitable delivery.
  • Oversee regional budget performance and present financial outcomes to regional and global stakeholders.

Regional insight and continuous improvement

  • Use performance data to identify risks, issues and improvement opportunities across the region.
  • Translate insight into action — ensuring key issues have clear owners, measurable outcomes and appropriate escalation routes.
  • Identify recurring operational bottlenecks and lead remediation, including regional adoption of global improvement initiatives.

Cross-functional partnership

  • Act as the key operational connector between EMEA and global operations capabilities.
  • Partner across Sales, Account, Implementation, Finance, HR, Technology and Offshore functions to drive client outcomes and operational consistency.
  • Provide regional operational input into sales pursuits, client mobilisation, scope expansions and solution design — ensuring proposed models are deliverable and scalable.
  • Interface with Global Programme Directors where regional and global client contexts intersect, aligning on dependencies, escalations and capacity impacts.

Team leadership and development

  • Lead, coach and develop the Regional Operations team, building a high-performing function with clear roles, standards and ways of working.
  • Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, operational discipline and continuous improvement.
  • Ensure the team has the skills, confidence and behaviours needed to support a more mature, insight-led and scalable delivery model. 

What you need to be great in this role: 

Essential

  • Senior operations leadership experience within, advertising, consulting, creative production, media agency or professional services.
  • Deep understanding of agency operating models — including client delivery, workflow, resource planning, utilisation, scopes of work, billing, compliance and margin management.
  • Proven experience leading regional or multi-market operations teams in a people-led, fast-paced environment.
  • Strong commercial acumen, with confidence managing the operational levers that affect profitability.
  • Experience owning or improving resource and capacity management, including demand and supply visibility, workforce mix and deployment planning.
  • Ability to use operational data, KPIs and reporting to identify risks, drive action and improve performance.
  • Track record embedding governance, process discipline and ways of working across complex teams or markets.
  • Strong cross-functional stakeholder skills — with experience partnering across regional and global functions including Finance, HR, Technology, Account and Delivery.
  • Proven people leadership: building capable teams, strengthening operational performance and creating a culture of accountability.
  • Comfortable moving between strategic direction and hands-on operational problem-solving.

Desirable

  • Experience in a global matrix organisation with regional, global and offshore delivery models.
  • Background in an in-house agency, embedded agency, creative production or complex marketing ecosystem.
  • Exposure to client mobilisation, implementation, transition or new operating model design.
  • Experience contributing to RFPs, commercial modelling, solution design or delivery model development.
  • Exposure to automation, AI-enabled operations, workflow optimisation or digital transformation in a marketing or agency environment.

Commercial and budget accountability

  • Experience overseeing regional or annual operational budgets and presenting financial performance to senior stakeholders.
  • Track record of driving margin discipline — reducing leakage, rework and avoidable cost across complex delivery environments.
  • Ability to connect operational decisions to commercial outcomes and communicate financial performance clearly to leadership.
  • Strategic integration of AI tools to improve operational efficiency, insight and reporting across a regional function.
  • Experience setting AI governance standards and embedding AI-assisted workflows within a team or function.
  • Agentic leadership approach: systematic, outcome-oriented problem-solving across complex, multi-stakeholder environments.
  • Confidence driving AI adoption and sharing best practice across a broader operations network.
  • Strong judgment in evaluating AI outputs and maintaining rigorous human oversight.

raw.description:
Established in 2004, OLIVER is the world's first and only specialist in designing, building, and running bespoke in-house agencies and marketing ecosystems for brands. We partner with over 300 clients in 40+ countries and counting. Our unique model drives creativity and efficiency, allowing us to deliver tailored solutions that resonate deeply with audiences. 

As a part of The Brandtech Group, we're at the forefront of leveraging cutting-edge AI technology to revolutionise how we create and deliver work. Our AI solutions enhance efficiency, spark creativity, and drive insightful decision-making, empowering our teams to produce innovative and impactful results. 

Role: Regional Operations Director (EMEA)

Location: London, United Kingdom (3 days a week from our London offices)

About the role: 

The Regional Operations Director is accountable for the operational effectiveness of the EMEA region. Reporting to the Global Chief Transformation and Operations Officer, you'll translate the global operating model into practical, market-specific execution — building the structure, governance and performance focus needed to strengthen operational control and support scalable growth.

You'll lead a regional operations team, partner closely with regional and global leadership, and act as the key connector between regional execution and global capability. The role calls for a leader equally comfortable setting strategic direction and solving complex operational problems hands-on — someone who turns data into action, builds high-performing teams, and keeps commercial performance firmly in focus.

What you will be doing: 

 

Regional operational leadership

  • Set clear priorities, accountabilities and ways of working for the EMEA Regional Operations function.
  • Build the structure, rhythm and capability needed to improve client delivery, business performance and regional growth.
  • Act as the senior operational partner to Regional Leadership on risks, performance, capacity and improvement priorities.

Client delivery operations

  • Own the operational run model for EMEA clients — including cadence, governance, issue resolution and escalation management.
  • Partner with Account Leadership to ensure delivery risks are visible, blockers are resolved quickly and client teams are set up to deliver effectively.
  • Ensure regional clients are mobilised and supported through consistent operating standards and reliable delivery controls.

Governance, cadence and decision management

  • Own the regional governance rhythm: forums, communications, decision-making and performance reviews.
  • Ensure decisions are made at the right level, escalations are routed effectively and regional context is represented in relevant global and regional forums.
  • Drive clear actions, accountability and follow-through across the function.

Operating model execution

  • Embed the global operating model across EMEA, ensuring standards, processes, tools and governance expectations are adopted consistently.
  • Translate enterprise-level standards into practical, market-specific ways of working.

Resource and capacity management

  • Own the regional view of demand, supply, utilisation, resource mix and capacity gaps.
  • Partner with Global Capacity Management, Account Teams, Delivery Leads and Offshore Operations to optimise deployment, resolve constraints and improve utilisation.
  • Provide regional input into enterprise workforce planning and future capacity needs.

Business and client enablement

  • Ensure regional client teams have the operational foundations needed to mobilise and deliver work effectively.
  • Coordinate core business processes including client onboarding, timesheeting, billing readiness, interagency set-ups, compliance and headcount approvals.
  • Act as the regional operational point of coordination for enablement issues, working across Finance, HR, Technology and Implementation to unblock dependencies.

Commercial performance and margin management

  • Manage the operational levers that affect cost-to-serve across the region, including scope leakage, resource efficiency, rework and avoidable cost.
  • Partner with Account Leadership and Finance to improve margin visibility and ensure practical actions are in place to protect profitable delivery.
  • Oversee regional budget performance and present financial outcomes to regional and global stakeholders.

Regional insight and continuous improvement

  • Use performance data to identify risks, issues and improvement opportunities across the region.
  • Translate insight into action — ensuring key issues have clear owners, measurable outcomes and appropriate escalation routes.
  • Identify recurring operational bottlenecks and lead remediation, including regional adoption of global improvement initiatives.

Cross-functional partnership

  • Act as the key operational connector between EMEA and global operations capabilities.
  • Partner across Sales, Account, Implementation, Finance, HR, Technology and Offshore functions to drive client outcomes and operational consistency.
  • Provide regional operational input into sales pursuits, client mobilisation, scope expansions and solution design — ensuring proposed models are deliverable and scalable.
  • Interface with Global Programme Directors where regional and global client contexts intersect, aligning on dependencies, escalations and capacity impacts.

Team leadership and development

  • Lead, coach and develop the Regional Operations team, building a high-performing function with clear roles, standards and ways of working.
  • Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, operational discipline and continuous improvement.
  • Ensure the team has the skills, confidence and behaviours needed to support a more mature, insight-led and scalable delivery model. 

What you need to be great in this role: 

Essential

  • Senior operations leadership experience within, advertising, consulting, creative production, media agency or professional services.
  • Deep understanding of agency operating models — including client delivery, workflow, resource planning, utilisation, scopes of work, billing, compliance and margin management.
  • Proven experience leading regional or multi-market operations teams in a people-led, fast-paced environment.
  • Strong commercial acumen, with confidence managing the operational levers that affect profitability.
  • Experience owning or improving resource and capacity management, including demand and supply visibility, workforce mix and deployment planning.
  • Ability to use operational data, KPIs and reporting to identify risks, drive action and improve performance.
  • Track record embedding governance, process discipline and ways of working across complex teams or markets.
  • Strong cross-functional stakeholder skills — with experience partnering across regional and global functions including Finance, HR, Technology, Account and Delivery.
  • Proven people leadership: building capable teams, strengthening operational performance and creating a culture of accountability.
  • Comfortable moving between strategic direction and hands-on operational problem-solving.

Desirable

  • Experience in a global matrix organisation with regional, global and offshore delivery models.
  • Background in an in-house agency, embedded agency, creative production or complex marketing ecosystem.
  • Exposure to client mobilisation, implementation, transition or new operating model design.
  • Experience contributing to RFPs, commercial modelling, solution design or delivery model development.
  • Exposure to automation, AI-enabled operations, workflow optimisation or digital transformation in a marketing or agency environment.

Commercial and budget accountability

  • Experience overseeing regional or annual operational budgets and presenting financial performance to senior stakeholders.
  • Track record of driving margin discipline — reducing leakage, rework and avoidable cost across complex delivery environments.
  • Ability to connect operational decisions to commercial outcomes and communicate financial performance clearly to leadership.
  • Strategic integration of AI tools to improve operational efficiency, insight and reporting across a regional function.
  • Experience setting AI governance standards and embedding AI-assisted workflows within a team or function.
  • Agentic leadership approach: systematic, outcome-oriented problem-solving across complex, multi-stakeholder environments.
  • Confidence driving AI adoption and sharing best practice across a broader operations network.
  • Strong judgment in evaluating AI outputs and maintaining rigorous human oversight.

raw.title: People Partner
raw.description:
About Radiant

Radiant is redefining how AI infrastructure is built.

We design and operate AI-native cloud platforms engineered for sovereignty, performance, and scale. Our infrastructure powers GPU-native workloads, multi-tenant control planes, and high-performance AI systems designed for the most demanding environments.

We are not building a generic cloud. We are building purpose-built AI infrastructure — from powered land, to compute, to software.

As we scale, we're building this organisation from the ground up. We're looking for people who'd rather build the playbook than inherit one — who are comfortable doing the work themselves as well as directing others, and who can adapt as fast as our strategy does. This is a startup model: attitude and adaptability matter more to us than years of experience or the size of the team you've previously managed.

The role

You’ll act as a trusted advisor to managers and employees, providing practical guidance and support across employee relations, performance management, manager coaching and the wider employee lifecycle. Combining hands-on HR expertise with a solutions-focused approach, you’ll help managers navigate complex people matters confidently, ensure consistent and compliant People practices across our global teams, and drive continuous improvement through data, technology and automation as Radiant continues to scale.

What You'll Do

  • Act as the day-to-day point of contact for employees and managers on HR questions across the full employee lifecycle: onboarding, policy interpretation, benefits, and performance management.

  • Managing employee relations, providing expert support and recommending appropriate actions to address queries or problems. Proactively reviewing data to spot employee relations trends and suggest solutions, coaching Managers to tackle issues early on.

  • Serve as the local first line of defense for compliance, ensuring strict adherence to UK labor laws, employment standards, site-specific contracts, and safety protocols.

  • Help coordinate and run core HR cycles: performance reviews, compensation planning, and engagement surveys, for the London office.

  • Draft, review and interpret employment contracts, variations and restrictive covenants.

  • Own the review and update of people policies and the employee handbook, keeping them compliant and easy to use.

  • Track legislative changes, including the Employment Rights Act reforms, and lead their implementation.

  • Maintain accurate employee records and HR systems, and help build out People processes and documentation as the team grows.

 

Compliance

 

  • Help ensure compliance with employment law and best practice across the UK, Europe and the US, in consultation with the HRBP and external counsel as needed.

  • Compliance and risk. Make sure People processes meet UK employment law, data protection requirements, our ISO requirements and Radiant's own policies. Ensure the team keeps policies and manager guidance up to date as legislation changes.

Immigration and visas

  • Manage Skilled Worker and other visa applications from assessment to approval, partnering with our external immigration lawyers.

  • Advise on global mobility as we expand into Europe.

Workforce planning

  • Partner with leaders to build headcount plans aligned to business priorities and budget.

  • Advise on organisation design, team structures and spans of control as teams scale.

  • Use people data from HiBob and Ashby to inform hiring, retention and capacity decisions.

Performance

  • Help design and run the performance reviews and calibration process.

  • Support managers to set clear goals, give regular feedback and manage underperformance through fair, well-documented processes.

  • Link performance outcomes to development, promotion and reward decisions.

What you'll bring

  • 5+ years in a People Partner, HR Business Partner or senior generalist role, ideally in a scaling tech or high-growth business.

  • Deep, current knowledge of UK employment law and confidence applying it to real situations.

  • CIPD Level 5 or 7, or an employment law qualification.

  • Confident and knowledgeable enough to manage employee relations issues independently, with sound judgement on when to escalate.

  • A proactive, solutions-oriented approach and a track record of taking initiative.

  • Exposure to multi-jurisdiction employment matters is an advantage.

  • Strong technical capability and data literacy, and comfort using data and technology to inform decisions and drive efficiency

Senior Early Talent & G&A Recruiter
raw.description:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you'll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that's shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you'll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

Samsara is on a mission to power the connected operations that keep the world moving. As our Senior Early Talent & G&A Recruiter in EMEA, you will lead Engineering Early Talent (New Grads and Interns) and G&A hiring across multiple businesses. You will partner with regional and global leaders, build sourcing strategies that work, and give every candidate a standout experience.

You should apply if these excite you:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your work helps keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores and workers home safely, as we digitize large sectors of the global economy.
  • High-Impact Role: Direct visibility and influence with regional and global business leaders in a fast-growing organisation.
  • You are the architect of your own career: Put in the work and this role won't be your last at Samsara, with countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft.
  • You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together and support each other, surrounded by a high-calibre team that pushes you to do your best.
  • Cutting-Edge Tools: Work with best-in-class, AI-forward recruiting technologies and data-driven strategies.

In this role, you will: 

  • Lead G&A hiring across EMEA: partner with a very diverse group of business leaders, plan hiring by function (Finance, People, Legal, IT), and switch context fast to keep every business moving.
  • Build our Early Talent programs in EMEA: lead local New Grad and Intern hiring, grow university relations and campus pipelines, and work with HQ on planning and execution and with local engineering leaders to hire early-career talent who meet our high bar.
  • Build creative sourcing strategies across LinkedIn, referrals and other channels, tailored to each function and market and backed by EMEA market intelligence.
  • Manage the pipeline from sourcing to onboarding, with an exceptional candidate experience.
  • Use data to refine recruiting strategy and influence hiring decisions.
  • Champion diversity, equity and inclusion through impactful hiring programs.
  • Work with People, Legal, Finance and Mobility to streamline hiring, including country-specific requirements.
  • Mentor peers and foster a culture of learning in the recruitment team.
  • Embed Samsara's cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale.

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • You have 6+ years of proven full-cycle recruiting experience, preferably in a tech organisation with a very high hiring bar.
  • You have proven experience building Early Talent programs, hiring for Engineering New Grads and Interns in UK (mandatory) and G&A roles (e.g. Finance, People, Legal, IT) in EMEA.
  • You communicate with key partners in a concise, professional and pro-active way.
  • You have exceptional stakeholder management abilities and executive presence, experienced working with a very diverse population of business leaders and switching context rapidly and comfortably.
  • Innovation mindset: you're comfortable implementing new tools, technologies, and methodologies.
  • AI - forward: we would like to see strong analytical skills when looking into hiring data and forecasting hiring needs. 
  • Optimising the use of the AI tools available to create a better candidate experience and efficient workflows. No AI slop.

An ideal candidate also has:

  • Deep understanding of EMEA talent market trends, turned into actionable strategies for each function.
  • Proven outbound sourcing for technical and specialist talent in a competitive market.

What's in it for you?

  • The chance to shape and build Samsara's teams across EMEA.
  • A high-visibility role: build connections and influence with Samsara's regional & global business leaders.
  • A passionate, innovative & AI-Forward team committed to excellence

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you're ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working 

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual's ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations 

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity

We use Tofu, a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara's Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

Fraudulent Employment Offers

Samsara is aware of scams involving fake job interviews and offers. Please know we do not charge fees to applicants at any stage of the hiring process. Official communication about your application will only come from emails ending in ----- ----- or ----- For more information regarding fraudulent employment offers, please visit our blog post here.

Graduate Sales Development Representative
raw.description:
Thanks for stopping by and learning more about this role at Sitemate! ✨🏗️

We’d love to hear from you 👩‍💻👩🏽‍💻🧑🏿‍💻👨🏻‍💻

📝 Overview

The Sales Development Representative is responsible for qualifying and routing inbound leads across two channels: self-service and inside sales. This role involves frequent engagement with prospects through phone calls, emails, live chat, and internal tools such as Slack and Salesforce. This role runs inside that same AI-native approach we build for customers. Leads and account data flow into an AI-populated Salesforce, so reps start from a clean, enriched pipeline instead of manual entry. Every call is coached live by ClaudeMate, giving real-time feedback on framing, objection handling, and next steps as the conversation happens. Success in the role is measured by the number of product demonstrations booked and completed, with a strong track record of team performance consistently meeting or exceeding monthly targets.

 

Room to grow, fast-tracked

We hire SDRs expecting you to grow past the role. “Grow from Within" is one of our leadership operating principles - meaning proven performance gets noticed and backed fast, and that managers and leaders are encouraged to gravitate towards internal promotions vs. external hires

For SDRs, that typically means a path to Account Executive within 9 to 12 months, based on performance, not tenure. One of our SDRs moved into a leadership role running Sales Development for all of North America within 8 months. Others have made the jump from SDR to Enterprise AE and describe the same pattern from the other side: "Sitemate is process-driven (everything engineered), so if you can learn and grow from these processes and you’re open to honest, constructive feedback while giving your best every day, you'll level up quickly".

Read more stories like these on People of Sitemate.

Employment:

  • Salary:

    • OTE Remuneration:

      • £49,500 (incl. Pension)

    • Base Salary:

      • £33,000

    • Commission:

      • £16,500

🔧 Day-to-Day

  • You will be qualifying and routing inbound leads through two channels; self service & inside sales

  • You’ll be spending most of your time with prospects across phone calls, emails and live chat on our website, as well as internal tools like slack and salesforce.

  • Your quota is measured by the number of demonstrations booked and completed at the subsequent stage of the process. Our current team in this role have achieved >=95% of their targets each month since starting

 

⚡ Challenges

  • Learning about the built world if you haven’t had any exposure to it - there are a lot of different types of companies and plenty of new terminologies to learn.

  • Up-skilling your call/phone and email skills - although we have plenty of examples for you to learn from during your onboarding.

  • Understanding SaaS financial acronyms and common terminology - if you have not worked in a SaaS company before, there is going to be a lot of metrics to learn. This cheat sheet is a good resource: The Ultimate SaaS Acronyms Cheat Sheet

  • We move very quickly, so you’ll need to be excited to come in and learn extremely fast.

 

✅ Who This Role is For

  • Ambitious individuals wanting to pursue a career in SaaS

  • People who thrive in a structured, high-agency, KPI-driven environment

  • Strong communicators who enjoy building relationships

  • Resilient individuals who can persevere and perform with high-volume tasks

 

🚫 Who This Role is Not For

  • Those unwilling to handle rejection frequently

  • People uncomfortable with people and conversations

 

🎯 Skills & Tools

Must Have:

  • Confident and clear communication skills, with excellent writing and presentation skills over email, phone, video conferencing and in-person.

  • Excellent task organization and prioritization skills, you’re able to multi-task efficiently.

Nice to Have:

  • Experience with modern tooling - CRMs, Health Scoring, Live chat, Knowledge bases.

  • Experience conducting customer meetings digitally (e.g. Zoom/Teams) and/or physically (in person/face to face with customers).

  • Patience working in an industry where not all users are tech-savvy.

About Sitemate:

Sitemate builds best-in-class software and AI agents for the built world, helping construction, infrastructure and industrial companies work smarter and faster. Our mission is to multiply the engineering power of the built world.

Storm is the #1 data capture agent for the front line of the built world - converting audio, photos and videos into clean structured records.

With conversational support in-app and across SMS, Whatsapp and phone calls, Storm is shifting front line workers from paperwork and clunky digital forms, to natural language and multi-channel data capture.

Our core platforms are Dashpivot (safety, quality and field reporting), Gearbelt (fleet and asset management), Flowsite (no-code integrations), and the Sitemate mobile app for every worker on site.

We have strong product-market fit, generating thousands of new leads per month through word of mouth and organic channels. We are backed by Blackbird, with 200 people across 18+ countries and entities in Australia, the UK, the US and Canada.

 

Life at Sitemate

At Sitemate, you’ll join a team that values transparency, high velocity, hustle, diversity, and innovation - not as buzzwords, but as the principles we work by every day.

We move fast, communicate openly, and operate with trust and autonomy. You’ll have access to key company metrics, clear career development plans, and the opportunity to grow your career based on performance, not tenure.

We believe diverse teams build better products. Our team includes members from 18+ countries - 55% identify as coming from underrepresented ethnic backgrounds, 43% identify as female, and our team spans ages 22–51.

 

Our Core Values

Our core values dictate “how we work”. We believe that basic human values such as honesty, trust and integrity are required to simply ‘get in the door’. Our values are designed to help us determine if an already great person, will be a great fit at Sitemate.

  • Handle with Care: Handle with thought and care, decisions are considered and consciously delivered

  • Everything Engineered: Everything engineered, intentional, planned and systematic

  • Quality Certified: Do it well, with attention to detail and accuracy, or don’t do it at all

  • Fast Tracked: Fast, incremental, and constant delivery of change

  • High Vis: A high visibility, transparent and  open environment

  • Rain, Hail or Shine: Show up for your team, your customers and yourself

Learn more about our values:

  • Read:

    • On Sitemate's Values, Culture and DNA

  • Listen:

    • Unleashing your Zilla

    • On scaling Sitemate, diversity, and culture

 

What We Offer

  • Competitive, performance-based remuneration

  • Equity options - own a piece of what you’re helping to build

  • 25 days paid annual leave, plus sick, carer’s, and compassionate leave

  • Parental leave - 16 weeks for primary and 6 weeks for secondary carers (including adoption and stillbirth support)

  • Learning & Development - professional growth budget and transparent career plans

  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP) - for confidential counseling, mental health support, and life resources

  • Laptop and home office setup budget

  • Flexible work - a hybrid rhythm, with 2 to 3 days in office, 2 WFH each week - with the flexibility to work from anywhere for several weeks a year

  • Community & Connection - weekly catered lunches, global offsites, and “Life Story” sessions

  • London office perks - large private outdoor terrace, on-site showers & bike storage, surrounded by cafés, galleries & vibrant nightlife in the heart of Shoreditch and a 5-minute walk to Old Street tube

 

Equal Opportunity

We’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer. Sitemate welcomes applicants of all genders, ethnicities, ages, sexualities, and abilities. Our team’s diversity is one of our greatest strengths, and we’re committed to ensuring an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive.

 

Learn More About Sitemate

🎧 Podcasts

  • 2026: CRO Lance Hodgson - on why the built world is jumping straight to AI and what that changes

  • 2024: CEO Hartley Pike - on scaling Sitemate, diversity, and culture

  • 2022: CTO Tim Bray - on building quality features that solve real customer problems

💬 Want to know what it’s like to work at Sitemate? Hear it straight from the team: People of Sitemate
⭐ Read what our customers say: G2 Crowd, Trust Radius
🎥 Team Offsites: 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025

PLEASE Note:

  • We hire directly and don’t work with agencies

Compensation: £49.5K • Offers Equity • £16.5K Commission • Base Salary: £33,000 & Commission: £16,500 (incl. Pension)

With conversational support in-app and across SMS, Whatsapp and phone calls, Storm is shifting front line workers from paperwork and clunky digital forms, to natural language and multi-channel data capture.

Our core platforms are Dashpivot (safety, quality and field reporting), Gearbelt (fleet and asset management), Flowsite (no-code integrations), and the Sitemate mobile app for every worker on site.

We have strong product-market fit, generating thousands of new leads per month through word of mouth and organic channels. We are backed by Blackbird, with 200 people across 18+ countries and entities in Australia, the UK, the US and Canada.

 

Life at Sitemate

At Sitemate, you’ll join a team that values transparency, high velocity, hustle, diversity, and innovation - not as buzzwords, but as the principles we work by every day.

We move fast, communicate openly, and operate with trust and autonomy. You’ll have access to key company metrics, clear career development plans, and the opportunity to grow your career based on performance, not tenure.

We believe diverse teams build better products. Our team includes members from 18+ countries - 55% identify as coming from underrepresented ethnic backgrounds, 43% identify as female, and our team spans ages 22–51.

 

Our Core Values

Our core values dictate “how we work”. We believe that basic human values such as honesty, trust and integrity are required to simply ‘get in the door’. Our values are designed to help us determine if an already great person, will be a great fit at Sitemate.

  • Handle with Care: Handle with thought and care, decisions are considered and consciously delivered

  • Fast Tracked: Fast, incremental, and constant delivery of change

  • High Vis: A high visibility, transparent and  open environment

What We Offer

raw.description:
Head of Partnerships (Africa)

Spending time in a hub location (London, Dubai, Paris, or New York) and Africa (50%+)

Shape the future of Africa’s financial landscape while building your legacy. This is your chance to lead business strategy, build powerful commercial relationships and directly drive positive outcomes for the continent and diaspora communities around the world.

You’ll have the freedom to trust your own instincts, make connections across Africa, and pursue commercial deals where your gut tells you opportunity exists. You’ll be trusted to know what’s best, to represent the business at senior levels, and to lead on some of our most critical relationships in the region.

Work for the market-leading emerging markets FinTech, with a genuine mission to support Africa's development by driving capital into the continent over the long term.

What you’ll do

As well as owning the relationship with existing partners in Africa, you'll constantly be identifying new partners and stakeholders in Africa, directly building relationships with them. You’ll negotiate great deals and oversee the process from first meeting to go-live.

Working with regulators and policy makers across the region, you’ll represent the Taptap Send brand externally, personifying competence and instilling confidence through all of your interactions.

Understanding everything that’s going on in your markets through the tracking, analysis, and reporting of key metrics will be key. You’ll also work with other members of the Growth team to develop and share best practices.

You’ll work cross-functionally with Product, Ops, Business Development, and Engineering teams to ensure Taptap Send has the best product offering in the market, being the internal voice of the region.

What you’ll need

  • ~10+ years of experience in high-performing, fast-paced environments (tech, professional services, finance etc)

  • A demonstrable instinct for commercial deal-making

  • Exposure to working with regulators and policy makers in Africa

  • Significant ties to Africa

  • “No task too small” mentality and willingness to delve into gritty details to get things done

  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills

Nice to have

  • Fluency in a language other than English (e.g. French), a plus

  • Experience in Financial Services, Fintech, Payments

About the company

Since our launch in 2019, we have transformed how money moves across borders with our operations spanning 6 out of 7 continents and covering both the busiest and most underserved (remittance) corridors. The next stage of growth will fuel a network of services and products especially designed to make money more accessible to diaspora communities including local cards, and additional savings and payments features.

We’re growing fast, backed by world-class investors, and scaling a product that blends real world impact with cutting edge fintech innovation.

 

Please click the ‘Apply’ button.

About Us

 

We’re building the world’s leading cross-border fintech for emerging markets - empowering families, fuelling local economies, and changing how millions access financial services.

 

Since our launch in 2019, we have transformed how money moves across borders with our operations spanning 6 out of 7 continents and covering both the busiest and most underserved (remittance) corridors. We tapped into a massive shift - from banks to phones - bringing digital finance to places where traditional systems never reached. The next stage of growth will fuel a network of services and products especially designed to make money more accessible to diaspora communities including local cards, and additional savings and payments features.

 

We’re growing fast, backed by world-class investors, and scaling a product that blends real world impact with cutting edge fintech innovation.

 

Here’s a little more:

  • Founded by Harvard grads and 3-time founders who previously built Segovia (acquired) and GiveDirectly (>$300M revenue, fastest-growing NGO in the world)

  • Backed by top investors including Spark Capital, Canaan, Reid Hoffman, Breyer Capital, Unbound, Wamda, and more

  • Built by global top performers from Bain, Google, McKinsey, Uber, Checkout, Bolt, and beyond - we move fast, stay humble, and care deeply about our mission

  • Truly global team - 250+ people, 50+ nationalities, 50+ languages

  • Guided by our values - ownership, impact, humility, and heart - in deed, not just word

Team next

Accept reality

Propose solutions

Win with grit

Be proactively candid, with yourself and others

Love the particular

Own it

raw.title: Product & Regulatory Counsel
raw.description:
Tired of meeting the product at the terms and conditions stage?

Most product lawyers see the flow once it's built and the launch date is set. Here, you're on the whiteboard at ideation, so compliant by design is the plan, not the clean-up.

And the stakes are real. Taptap Send moves billions of dollars every month across 100 countries, and is now building wallets, cards and broader financial products for diaspora communities.

The job

You'll advise on new licensing and products from first idea to go-live, and own regulator engagement across our markets.

  • Shape products before they're built: review designs, UX, flows and terms against regulatory and customer-outcome rules, Consumer Duty included, while change is still cheap.

  • Turn regulation into decisions: what's mandatory, what's prudent, and the alternative route that still gets it launched.

  • Own the regulator relationship: across our markets, including new ones, and flag what regulatory change means for the roadmap early.

  • Take products to new countries: localise what already works, with country leads and local counsel.

  • Build the playbooks: templates that let Legal scale without adding friction.

Why you'll want it

Spend your time on the hard questions. You're asked to shape our roadmap and launches, and understand how to fit them to the relevant regimes

Be a peer, with room to run. You'll join a flat team of regulatory and commercial lawyers, with real autonomy and a manager who trusts you.

Make launches faster, not slower. Legal in the room from day one is how products here ship sooner. That's the whole point of your seat.

Make sending money home cheaper. Remittances pay for school fees, rent and medical bills, and are worth more than all foreign aid combined. Cheaper, reliable transfers put more of that money in families' hands.

Is this you?

You're a qualified lawyer (UK or equivalent) with 4+ years' PQE in payments, e-money or financial services regulation, at a firm, a regulator or a fintech.

You've advised payments or e-money firms under the FCA or an equivalent regime, dealt with the regulator directly, and helped product teams take live launches over the line.

You give the answer first and the reasoning second. Ambiguity across several jurisdictions doesn't stop you making the call.

If you'd rather be asked first than asked last, apply. Missing a box or two? Send your CV anyway.

raw.title: Python Software Engineer
raw.description:
About Abound

We’re redefining consumer lending in the UK, and beyond. Using advanced AI and Open Banking data, we make fair, affordable personal finance available to more people. While traditional lenders rely almost entirely on credit scores, we look at the full financial picture - how much you spend, and what you can afford to repay to build a deeper, more accurate understanding of each customer's unique financial situation.


And we've shown it works at scale. We’ve issued over £1.3bn in loans directly to customers while delivering market-leading credit performance - for every 10 defaults the industry expects, we see only 3. We also reached profitability just 2.5 years after launch.


Backed by £2bn+ of funding from top-tier investors including Citi, GSR Ventures, and Deutsche Bank, we’re recognised as one of Europe’s fastest-growing fintechs (Sifted, CNBC). Now, we’re expanding into new markets and product lines - and we’re looking for ambitious people who want to learn fast, take ownership, and grow with us.

About the role

We’re looking for a Software Engineer to help us build high-quality, reliable backend systems that accelerate our mission.

This role sits within our mortgage engineering team. You’ll work across the backend stack, owning features end to end: from shaping product and technical requirements through implementation, launch, and iteration.

This role is ideal for a hungry, ambitious engineer who wants to step up quickly; someone with strong engineering fundamentals, high ownership, and the drive to grow into a senior-level contributor.

What you’ll be doing:

  • Build and ship high-quality backend features using Python, Django, RESTful APIs, GraphQL, Pydantic, Postgres, and Google Cloud

  • Own backend work from concept through delivery, including technical design, implementation, testing, deployment, and iteration

raw.description:
About Adclear

At Adclear, we're building the trust layer for how the world's most regulated companies bring products to market. Every bank, lender and investment platform runs into the same invisible pain: compliance review that slows down every campaign, every launch, every idea. We're turning the function that has always said 'no' into infrastructure that says 'yes, and here's how'.

This is a fundamental shift in how regulated industries and compliance teams operate, and we're only at the beginning. The product you'll design is what people actually touch when they experience that shift.

Founded in 2024, we've already earned the trust of leading innovators as well as established enterprises including Monzo, Lloyds, PensionBee, Kraken, Coinbase and many others. Our early traction let us raise 2.6m in funding, and we're now scaling fast. We're building the product engine that turns a genuinely novel category into something people love to use, and this is where you come in.

The Role

This is a full-stack product role with real scope: you won't be handed a corner of a system, you'll own complete product slices end-to-end, from spec through to something live that customers depend on every day. Here's a taste of what that looks like in practice:

  • A Chrome extension that runs compliance checks inline in Google Docs, where marketers actually write copy. Built with Monzo as the design partner. Public on the Chrome Web Store.

  • A natural-language copilot for compliance work. Users ask in plain English, the platform proposes typed actions, a human approves, the action runs. Not chat over a database.

  • The interface where reviewers watch the model reason through a decision, step in when they disagree, and feed structured corrections back into the rules.

  • An integration surface that reaches into wherever customers create marketing: Canva, Figma, Google Docs, Contentful, Workfront, Monday.com, Frame.io for video.

  • A dashboard that takes a long, unsorted list of compliance tasks and turns it into a single prioritised queue.

You think in user outcomes and shipped work, not tickets closed. Your code handles edge cases, your APIs have clean contracts, and the work you ship stays shipped. Our users are compliance and marketing teams at leading fintechs. They use Adclear every day, and they'll tell you fast when something's wrong, which is exactly the kind of feedback loop that makes this job good.

What you'll do

  • Own product delivery. Take features from spec to production, frontend-first but covering backend and integration where needed.

  • Build the product surfaces compliance reviewers live in: workflows, review UIs, the moments where model output meets human judgement.

  • Work with AI in the critical path. Ship features where the model is genuinely part of the product, not a bolted-on feature.

  • Ship a change to production on your first day and a feature in your first week. We deploy continuously, so you'll feel the pace immediately.

  • Have real input on what we build, how we build it, and which problems are worth solving next. Nobody here is precious about a roadmap someone else wrote.

What we're looking for

  • Independent delivery. You can own and ship end-to-end product slices with minimal supervision. Your track record shows features that shipped, stuck, and solved real user problems.

  • Product trade-off judgement. You balance speed, quality and user impact under ambiguity. You push back when something is underspecified, and make pragmatic calls when it needs to ship anyway.

  • Product taste. You notice when something feels wrong and aren't afraid to raise it. You care about the smaller details while still knowing when to ship at pace.

  • Cross-functional pragmatism. You work effectively with founders, designers and AI engineers, and you unblock yourself rather than waiting on someone else.

  • AI literacy. You're fluent with modern coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, agents). You treat them as collaborators, know when to trust them and when to override them, and have real opinions about where they help and where they get in the way.

Strong technical depth in:

  • Building products where AI is in the critical path.

  • Modern web tooling. Node, Postgres.

Nice to have

  • Experience with Cloudflare Workers, Hono, or Drizzle.

  • Experience in regulated industries: fintech, healthtech, legaltech.

The Stack

React and TypeScript on the frontend. A Hono API on Cloudflare Workers. Drizzle and Postgres on the data layer.

Applied Intuition is scaling quickly across entities and geographies, and statutory reporting, clean audits, and compliant local filings are essential. Reporting to the Director of Accounting, you will lead the EMEA local close and statutory audits, own the filing calendar, oversee the US GAAP to local GAAP conversion work produced by our India-based outsourced accounting team, and partner with Tax, Legal, and Business Technology to automate statutory and compliance processes in NetSuite. At Applied Intuition, you will:

  • Own the EMEA statutory and compliance filing calendar, covering VAT, corporate income tax and zakat (with Tax and external advisers), company registry filings, and annual accounts, so every filing goes in on time with no notices from authorities.

  • Manage the quality and performance of our India-based outsourced accounting team and of in-country auditors, tax advisers, and accounting providers, and turn statutory and conversion workpapers into standard templates the team can run with minimal rework.

  • Partner with Business Technology to automate statutory reporting, VAT, and e-invoicing in NetSuite, design and document the related controls, and bring new entities and regulatory changes (for example, FRS 102 amendments and German and Saudi e-invoicing mandates) into the process ahead of effective dates.

We’re looking for someone who has:

  • Qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA, CIMA, or CPA) with 14+ years of relevant accounting experience

  • Proven ownership of multi-entity UK statutory reporting under UK GAAP (FRS 102) and the Companies Act 2006, including leading statutory audits end to end

  • Experience converting US GAAP to local GAAP and reviewing GAAP bridge workpapers (for example, leases and accrued vacation)

  • Experience managing outsourced or offshore accounting teams, including setting quality standards and reviewing output across time zones

  • Proficiency with NetSuite, ideally in a multi-subsidiary environment

  • Sound judgment on materiality and filing risk, and clear communication with auditors, advisers, and partners across EMEA, the US, and India

Nice to have:

  • Big 4 or top-tier public accounting background, and in-house experience at a software/technology multinational

  • Hands-on German GAAP (HGB) and GmbH statutory experience

  • Exposure to Swedish (K2/K3) or Saudi (IFRS, zakat, ZATCA e-invoicing) statutory reporting, or other EMEA local GAAPs and languages

  • Working knowledge of VAT, Making Tax Digital, and e-invoicing requirements across EMEA

The world's largest companies compete by being different, and most of that difference lives in software they built for themselves. It is also the hardest thing in the business to change safely, so good ideas wait months, sometimes years, for the systems to catch up.

We are a talent-dense team doing our life's work in London and New York. Extreme ownership, high velocity, low-ego collaboration. What you build here shapes the company, and how the world's largest companies operate.

About the role

We're looking for someone to own employer brand and talent community as part of the founding marketing team. Hiring exceptional people fast enough is the biggest challenge Conduct faces. We're scaling from about 70 people to 500, across engineering, deployment strategy, go-to-market and operations, and every one of those candidates needs to understand why Conduct matters.

You will articulate why Conduct matters to talent: who we are, what we care about, why the product matters and where it is going. Who we hire

We work with some of the largest enterprises in the world, and security is core to earning and keeping that trust. This is a builder's role as much as an operator's: you'll design and ship the security features our enterprise customers need, not just run controls and tooling.

You'll stand out if you:

  • Have shipped security features as a software engineer - things like BYOK per tenant, SSO/SCIM, or SIEM-compatible audit logging - not just configured or audited them

  • Have hands-on experience with enterprise security requirements - completing security questionnaires, navigating customer requirements around data handling and contractual agreements

You'll own our security posture end to end: the day-to-day operational work of keeping us secure, the security capabilities our enterprise customers demand, and the bigger initiatives on our security roadmap as we build out the function. Day to day, you'll:

  • Design and build security features that ship in our product - like BYOK per tenant, SIEM-compatible audit logs, and SSO/SCIM - working directly in the codebase alongside product engineers

  • Own enterprise security end to end - completing customer security questionnaires, working through requirements around data handling and contractual agreements, and acting as the technical point of contact for our clients’ CISOs and security teams

  • Monitor and harden our cloud environment - tracking security recommendations, driving remediation, and making pragmatic risk-acceptance calls where they're justified

  • Investigate and respond to security alerts across our endpoint, cloud, and application stack

  • Build out our detection and monitoring capabilities, evolving our SIEM with alerting that cuts through the noise

  • Own vulnerability management end to end - triaging, tracking, and driving issues through to resolution

  • Proactively hunt for threats, from unusual behaviour in our environment to emerging risks like package and supply chain compromises

  • Run and refine security scanning across our infrastructure, applications, and dependencies

Who we hire

  • Background can come from any type of security engineering; what matters most is that you're comfortable reading and writing code - you'll be building product features and tooling, not just operating them

raw.title: Commercial Lead
raw.description:
About Griffin

Hi, we’re Griffin. We’re a fully regulated UK bank that powers the accounts and payments offerings of product-led fintechs and platforms like Uber, Yonder, Prosper, and Sidekick. By doing the heavy lifting behind the scenes, our customers can focus on what they do best - delivering amazing customer experiences.

We’ve grown rapidly since our launch in 2024, and today provide the banking backbone behind products in remittance, payroll, wealth, insurance, proptech, payments, neobanking and more.

We’re moving into card issuing, stablecoin infrastructure, and agentic finance next as we continue to support the next generation of product-led companies.

Learn more about what we do

Our culture

We believe that smart, motivated, conscientious people thrive in high-trust, high-autonomy environments and have done our best to create such an environment at Griffin. People who thrive here don’t require much hand-holding, and go out of their way to figure out how to contribute in the most valuable way possible.

We've been remote-first since we were established in 2017 and we remain so today. Work here is asynchronous and fully flexible - because we want to be a part of your life in a way that helps you to get the most out of both your work and home life.

We understand that our culture and ways of working aren’t for everyone, and we’re very intentional about our hiring process as a result. We won't hire people who don’t seem like a strong fit for our core values, even if they're otherwise extremely qualified.

Our strong culture has helped us to remain a mission-driven company as we have scaled, and gives our people a clear, explicit operating framework and the space to focus on delivering real value for our customers.

Learn more about our culture.

The team

We’re the Connect team, what most companies call Sales. We strive to bring the best in technology, user experience and banking to the embedded finance space and be the bank for fintechs and corporates to build on.

We’re 10 people across Commercial, Customers Success and Marketing, led by Phoebe, our Chief Revenue Officer and we’re currently focused on winning new businesses and selecting the right customers to partner with for long term mutual success.

The opportunity

You’ll take Griffin’s licensed bank and banking-as-a-service proposition to mid-market and enterprise companies in payments, lending, proptech, vertical SaaS, insurtech and digital assets. You’ll own each deal from first lead to signed commercial terms. You’ll show their engineering, product, risk and compliance teams how it all works, from API architecture and safeguarding to ledger flows, and talk with confidence to their CFO, COO or CTO. You’ll build your own pipeline, shape pricing for complex accounts with RevOps and Finance, and work with Legal, Compliance and Product on bespoke client needs. Think solutions architect who closes.

What success looks like

Within 12 months, you’ll have built a pipeline you sourced yourself, with deals that are bigger and more structured as you go. Prospects’ CFOs and CTOs will trust you to explain how it all works, and Legal, Compliance and Product will bring you in early on every non-standard deal.

To do this you’ll own

  • Your pipeline, from first lead to signed commercial terms, including sourcing your own leads alongside whatever SDRs and marketing bring in

  • Whiteboard sessions on account structures, and the technical proposal content, which you’ll write yourself

  • Pricing and commercial structures for complex accounts, such as consumption-based or bundled models, tiered volume and transfer pricing, built with RevOps and Finance

  • Regulatory and compliance questions, answered before they turn into objections

  • Commercial and technical arrangements for non-standard client requirements, shaped with Legal, Compliance and Product

Your background

To ensure this, we’re looking for people who have:

  • Built and closed their own pipeline, and get their energy from chasing and winning new business

  • A strong grasp of payments and banking infrastructure (settlement, safeguarding, ledgers, APIs, card and account issuing) and enough regulatory knowledge (EMI versus bank licence, Consumer Duty, safeguarding rules) to hold a credible conversation with a compliance team

  • Sold complex deals with long cycles and several buying committees, and negotiated beyond simple discounting, including pricing models, volume commitments and contractual carve-outs

  • A low ego and high curiosity, with a real appetite for understanding how the plumbing works

  • The resilience for long, technical sales cycles, and the confidence to work without a fixed script while our products and structures evolve

  • A love of writing - we have a major amount of written documentation that you will be contributing to, and we place a high degree of importance on clarity and readability (you can find out more here about how we write)


Nice to haves

Ideally, you would also:

  • Have worked at a BaaS provider, EMI or challenger bank, including in an SMCR-regulated environment

  • Have a structuring background, such as transaction structuring, treasury or Big 4 financial services advisory

What can we offer you?

We are an early stage startup and we're working hard to expand our benefits package. We're planning to add to this list in the future.

  • Salary: Up to £100,000 + commission

  • Remote-first flexibility: Work from anywhere in the UK. However, for this role you will need to be comfortable with regular travel to London, often at short notice.

  • Work from abroad: Up to 20 days a year

  • Time off: 25 days’ holiday, bank holidays and a winter break (we shut down between Christmas and New Year)

  • Share options: Own a part of what we’re building together

  • Pension: Auto-enrolment into our Penfold scheme

  • Insurance: Private medical with Bupa (including family cover) and life insurance with AIG

  • Wellbeing: 1:1 coaching and therapy session available through Oliva

  • Family leave: Enhanced parental leave with up to 6 months on full pay after two years’ service

  • AI tools: Everyone has a Claude subscription on us and access to other premium tools

  • Your setup: We’ll support you in creating a comfortable and effective WFH environment.

How long will the process take?

We move as fast as possible, but it normally takes us about 2-3 weeks to get to know to each other.

  • Step 1: An initial phone call with our Talent Team for us to tell you more about Griffin and learn about your recent experience.

  • Step 2: Meet your manager to talk through your experience and how that relates to the requirements.

  • Step 3: A task based on what you’ll be doing on a day to day at Griffin.

  • Step 4: Meet with peers in your team for a more in-depth technical interview.

  • Step 5: Pitch the Founder and CRevO

  • Step 6: Culture interview: Learn more about this here.

As a bank, we’re committed to maintaining the highest standards of security. This means that the successful candidate will need to complete background screening, and our offer will be conditional upon satisfactory review of these checks. This would include verification of right to work, criminal record, credit history, social media and professional reference checks

How do I apply?

Are we your next move? Apply via the link below, if there's a match our Talent team will reach out to schedule an initial conversation and talk you through what happens next.

Under representation

At Griffin, we’re looking for people who instinctively vibe with our values, behaviours and mission. You’re encouraged to apply, even if your experience doesn’t tick every box. Careers, like life, can take many twists and turns. Your technical expertise and path to where you are today will stand out. We're committed to creating a place where everyone belongs and we welcome diverse perspectives, backgrounds and people who are ready to build a global platform for programmable finance

Griffin Bank Ltd request that recruitment agencies do not speculatively submit CVs to any employee or associate of our company unless explicitly asked to do so by a member of our Talent team.

Any CVs sent to any member of our team on a speculative basis will not be recognised and we will not accept liability for any fee or commission should we subsequently employ a candidate who applied to us directly or was introduced by an instructed agency that may also have been submitted speculatively by an uninstructed agency.

About the role

This role is for someone wanting to start a career in operations within a financial services firm. You'll join as a Graduate focused on working complaints and train to become a fully competent Complaints Officer, investigating and resolving our more complex customer interactions across loans, cards and auto-finance. A critical role to help the business understand how it can serve customers better.

This is a casework role. From early on you will hold your own caseload, speak to customers directly, make decisions on whether we got it right, and put things right where we didn't. You will be supported through structured training, coaching and quality feedback as you develop in the role

Some of the areas you'll delve into are:

  • The regulatory framework for complaints: FCA regulation, the DISP rules, Consumer Duty, and how the guidance is applied to real cases.

  • Investigation technique: gathering evidence, interrogating system records and call recordings, and testing what actually happened against what should have happened.

  • Decision making and redress: reaching fair and objective outcomes, and calculating and explaining any compensation due.

  • Customer communication: writing final response letters that break complex issues down into plain English.

  • The Financial Ombudsman Service: how cases are referred, how FOS reaches its view, and how we apply those learnings to future cases.

  • Root cause and feedback: spotting the product and process failures behind complaints and feeding them back to frontline and product teams.

Reporting to a Complaints Manager within the Operations Team, you will be responsible for a live caseload and for the quality of the decisions you make on it.

No prior complaints experience needed, we care about how you think, not what you already know. This role requires an ability to learn quickly, work to deadlines and support our customers effectively.

Your team's objectives

raw.title: Data Architect
raw.description:
🍊Our mission

Great science regularly stalls in the clinic, not because the science is wrong, but because the company behind it lacks the capital, infrastructure, or focus to take it all the way through. Today’s clinical-stage biopharma model is broken, and as a result promising treatments never reach patients.

Our mission is to fix this: we’re building the next generation of biopharma by in-licensing clinical-stage therapeutic assets and developing them through Lindus Health’s integrated, technology-first clinical trial infrastructure. We’re a new initiative, but we’re building on a proven foundation - the same infrastructure that has delivered 82% of Lindus Health’s sponsor trials on or ahead of timeline, across 40+ completed trials across the US and Europe.

We’re in-licensing 5-7 clinical-stage, typically Phase-2-ready assets, funded directly from Lindus Health’s balance sheet. We’re targeting deal close on our first assets through 2026, with first trials launching in H1 2027.

🍊About the role

The Data Architect owns assigned studies end-to-end, taking full responsibility for both the design of the database on Citrus and the quality of the data it produces, from study planning through database lock. The role designs with the final analysis in mind, writes code where manual review would slow delivery, and designs the edit checks and validation that prevent issues before they make their way downstream. The Data Architect is the technical and data lead for assigned studies and works with Clinical Operations, Biostatistics, Programme Directors, and Product to ensure each study captures the data its scientific objectives require.

One person owns the database from study planning through lock, so the design and the data it produces never drift apart. The role also shapes how data delivery on Citrus develops, identifying where manual work can be automated.

🍊About you

  • You have around 5+ years of experience across clinical data management and/or trial platform design, with hands-on involvement in study setup, data review, and database lock

  • You can design a study's data capture on an EDC platform and define its specification: you understand edit checks and validation, and you can see how a design decision today could become a data quality problem later

  • You work with data programmatically, or are ready to build that skill quickly: Python, R, or SQL are used daily in this role, and you are expected to learn them on the job if you do not already have them

  • You have working knowledge of CDISC standards, particularly CDASH, with SDTM familiarity a plus, and you design with analysis-ready data in mind

  • You have experience with external data transfers and reconciliation

  • You understand GCP, ICH E6 and 21 CFR Part 11 and apply them in day-to-day decisions

  • You apply AI and automation responsibly to improve the quality and speed of data work in a regulated setting

  • You have a track record of working well across functions, especially Clinical Operations, Biostatistics, Programme Directors, and Product

  • You thrive in a startup environment that challenges the norms of typical biotechs, with high agency and a bias for action

  • You are passionate about our mission: changing how the healthcare industry operates and how new health treatments are developed

🍊What you’ll focus on

  • Own your assigned studies end-to-end, from defining critical data items and the data management plan through to database lock

  • Own the design of your studies on Citrus, utilizing AI combined with your expert review to translate protocol requirements into a specification and edit check logic that capture clean, analysis-ready data, and sign off that the design meets the protocol before go-live

  • Assess feasibility and flag complexity and risk early, where a design choice could affect data integrity, participant safety or study endpoints

  • Manage the full query lifecycle from generation through resolution, working directly with sites

  • Lead proactive, risk-based data review, automated where possible, to keep key study milestones on track, building repeatable checks rather than one-off reports

  • Use scripting and AI tooling day-to-day to automate data review, flag anomalies, and surface issues earlier, applied responsibly within validation, GCP and 21 CFR Part 11 expectations

  • Own fixes and change requests on your own studies during conduct, assessing their impact and the level of testing and sign-off required

  • Perform ongoing safety data review and facilitate medical coding (MedDRA, WHODrug) with the medical team

  • Build reports using programmatic data access (Python, R, SQL), delivered accurately and on schedule

  • Conduct all activities in line with relevant regulations and Lindus SOPs, keep study documentation to a standard that holds up under audit or inspection, and support auditors and inspectors on your studies where needed

  • Report bugs and usability issues, and feed operational insight back to Product to improve how Citrus supports data delivery

Make an impact across all areas of our business and fix one of the world's most broken industries.

  • Competitive salary, plus meaningful stock options

  • 27 days annual leave in addition to 11 National Holidays

  • Health insurance coverage through our PEO Trinet

  • $40 monthly wellness allowance, which you can spend on a wellhub membership, or wellness activities and expenses of your choice!

  • Regular whole company and team events, both in person and virtually

raw.description:
TL;DR

The Partner Marketing team extends Lovable’s reach by educating, engaging, and enabling partners globally to build market awareness and generate demand for their Lovable-powered solutions and services. We recruit prospective partners and support the onboarding and growth of existing ones as they build, launch, market, and scale their businesses through the Lovable Partner Ecosystem. We work closely with GTM partnerships, product partnerships, sales, and product marketing, and serve partner types from major technology and platform partners to the connectors, agencies, and independent experts who build with Lovable every day.

Why Lovable?

For decades, the ability to build software belonged to a tiny fraction of the population: the people with the credentials, the technical training, the access. Everyone else had to wait, or pay, or give up. Lovable is the counterargument: We exist for the people with ideas who were locked out of software creation until now.

Over 70 million projects have been built on the platform. Hundreds of thousands of people pay for it. The product handles real infrastructure, not only prototypes: authentication, databases, payments, and deployment. People run real businesses on Lovable, which means the stakes are real too.

The comms challenge: when anyone can build, the platform has to be safe for everyone who does, and they need to know it. That takes someone who can tell the story of how we think about topics like safety, security, and reliability before anyone asks, and who can be honest, precise, and fast when the questions come up anyway.

What you’ll do

  • You’re an adaptable generalist who thrives when shifting gears across commercial, analytical, operational, and client-facing tasks in a single day.
